It is also customary for the sevakas to give the prasadi twig afterwards as an honor to some special person. On that particular day, they gave this bakul twig to Mahaprabhu. The Lord was ecstatic at this sign of Jagannath’s grace and planted it in the ground at Hari Das’ place of bhajan. The twig eventually grew into a large tree under which Hari Das often sat to chant the Holy Names.

During the period when Hari Das Thakur’s successor Siddha Jagannath Das Goswami was the math’s mahant, the king sent people to cut down the tree, as extra wood was needed for the Rathayatra carts. Jagannath Das tried to dissuade them from doing so, citing the tree’s sacred origins and its association with the memory of Mahaprabhu and Hari Das. When Jagannath Das saw that his entreaties were falling on deaf ears, he finally gave up, taking it as Lord Jagannath’s desire. The king’s representatives told Jagannath Das that they would come the next day to cut down the tree, but that night, it suddenly became hollow. Naturally, the tree became useless as a provider of wood, and so the sacrilegious act was called off. From then on, the tree was named “siddha bakul.”

It is said that the Lord planted the twig on the first day of the Orissan month of Chaitra, also known as Maha Vishuva Sankranti. In memory of this event, a festival named the *Danta-kāṣṭha-ropaṇa Mahotsava* is held on that day ever year. As a part of the ritual, the tree is given a formal bath with 108 jugs of water.

The extraordinary beauty of this tree enchants all devotee pilgrims. They pay their obeisances to this spiritual desire tree with all the devotion at their command and beg the Supreme Lord, the spiritual master and the Vaishnavas to give them a taste for chanting the Holy Name.

## The temple

The temple building houses a wooden murti of Mahaprabhu in his six-armed form, flanked by Nityananda on His right and Advaita Acharya on his left., and deities of Radha-Govinda. There is also a wooden murti of Hari Das Thakur, which is not in the deity room itself, but in a shrine just outside it, in the Jagamohan. Hari Das is seated and holds a japa mala in his hand, chanting the Holy Names as he did throughout his life. Beside it, there is another small shrine dedicated to Lakshmi and Narayan. On the north side of the temple, directly attached to the building, is shrine dedicated to Lord Nrisingha. This shrine has been there since before Hari Das came to live there.

At one time there was a good manuscript library in the Math, but sometime in the early part of the 20thcentury it was regrettably neglected and many valuable books were lost. One of those manuscripts was an Orissan verse translation of the Srimad Bhagavatam by Dina Krishna Das. This translation was especially dear to Gaudiya Vaishnavas, who felt it was better written and truer to the Bhagavata’s teachings than the more generally used Oriyan Bhagavata written by Atibori Jagannath Das. Unfortunately, no copies of this translation can be found anywhere any more. Other rare books in this library included *Gaura-kṛṣṇodaya*, an original biography of Mahaprabhu written by the Orissan poet Govinda Deva.

## Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati at Siddha Bakul

When Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Prabhupada came to Jagannath Puri in 1936, the mahant of Siddha Bakul Math, Srimat Balabhadra Das Goswami, came to meet him at the Purushottam Math to invite him to speak there on the Srimad Bhagavatam for a few days. Part of their conversation was recorded in the *Gaudiya*, the weekly Bengali periodical of the Gaudiya Math.

Srila Prabhupada said, “Siddha Bakul is where Hari Das Thakur lived, but just as importantly, it is also the place where Rupa Goswami stayed.” He then went on to discuss how Rupa Goswami was able to understand Mahaprabhu’s mind. He concluded, “Without both taking shelter of the Namacharya and being a follower of Rupa Goswami, we cannot get the mercy of Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.”

The mahant replied, “Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur first wrote about Siddha Bakul in his *Jaiva Dharma*. The *Hari-nāma-cintāmaṇi* contains Hari Das Thakur’s instructions on the Holy Name, which were also given under the Siddha Bakul.”

Srila Prabhupada said, “When Rupa Goswami was living with Hari Das Thakur at Siddha Bakul, then Mahaprabhu would come daily to see him and talk about Krishna. Rupa Goswami wrote his play, *Vidagdha-mādhava*, while staying here. When Mahaprabhu heard the *tuṇḍe tāṇḍavinī ratiṁ vitanute* verse, He was inundated with feelings of ecstatic love. There is no verse that more beautifully illustrates the glories of the Holy Name.

“On another day, Mahaprabhu came to Siddha Bakula with Ramananda Raya, Svarupa Damodara, Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya and other members of his entourage. He praised Rupa’s verses to them all. Ramananda Raya asked Rupa Goswami to read the verses to his chosen deity that open the *Vidagdha-mādhava.* Rupa read his famous verse glorifying Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, *anarpita-carīṁ cirāt karuṇayāvatīrṇaḥ kalau.* It is as though Siddha Bakul is the spring from which two rivers of nectar -- Hari Das Thakur’s nectar of Harinam Sankirtan and Rupa Goswami’s nectar of transcendental poetry -- overflowed and washed Gaura Hari’s lotus feet. Mahaprabhu’s devotees led by Svarupa and Ramananda relished all this ambrosia with him, to their great delight.”

## The disciplic succession at the Math

This math is also not without controversy. The guru-parampara of the Siddha Bakul Math is given by those currently in charge as follows –

1\. Sri Krishna Chaitanya Mahaprabhu  
2\. Srila Hari Das Thakur  
3\. Siddha Sri Jagannath Das  
4\. Sri Narahari Das Mahant Goswami  
5\. Sri Gaura Hari Das  
6\. Radha Mohan Das  
7\. Gopi Mohan Das  
8\. Bhagavan Das  
9\. Gopi Charan Das  
10\. Shyama Charan Das  
11\. Sadhu Charan Das  
12\. Narahari Das  
13\. Balaram Das  
14\. Paramananda Das  
15\. Balabhadra Das  
16\. Srinivas Das

Siddha Jagannath Das was a very powerful Vaishnava. His reputation reached the king of Puri, who wished to donate a great deal of land to the Math. Jagannath Das refused these gifts, however, saying that he preferred to serve the deities with whatever he could beg through the madhukari system. After Sri Narahari Das, all the abbots of this Math have been given the title “Mahant Goswami.” According to Balabhadra Das, the temple management changed hands at the time of Bhagavan Das. His successor, Gopi Charan Das Mahant Goswami, started accepting land holdings in the name of the Deity.

The Radha Kanta Math does not accept the above parampara. Its authorities give the following history of the math according to their records: Since the Siddha Bakul Math was formerly Kashi Mishra’s garden, it was originally part of the Radha Kanta Math. It was given the name Siddha Bakul because Hari Das Thakur attained perfection (i.e., left his body) under this bakul tree. The original Mahant of Radha Kanta Math was Vakreshwar Pandit Goswami; he was succeeded by Gopal Guru Goswami, whose disciple was Dhyana Chandra Goswami, who was followed by Balabhadra Goswami. Balabhadra had two disciples – Dayanidhi and Bhagavan Das. Balabhadra gave Bhagavan Das responsibility for the Siddha Bakul Math, which was given independent status as the sixteenth branch (*adhikāri-maṭha*) math of the Radha Kanta Math. According to this account, Bhagavan Das was the first mahant of the Siddha Bakul Math. Bhagavan Das was succeeded by Gopal Charan Das, Shyam Charan Das, Sadhu Charan Das, Narahari Das, Balaram Das, Paramananda Das, and Balabhadra Das, respectively. The present mahant is thus in the twelfth generation after Vakreshwar Pandit.

According to the Radha Kanta Math, the tilak and other symbols of the parampara coming from Vakreshwar were used in the Siddha Bakul Math until 1942 when they were changed by Balabhadra Das. To further support their claims, the Radha Kanta Math points to the tradition that whenever a new mahant was named at Siddha Bakul, the mahant of the Radha Kanta Math would be present and would give him a special gift.

In the *Gaudiya* magazine, the following comment is found about the unorthodoxy of the Siddha Bakul Math in the 1930’s: “Hari Das Thakur preached the pure practice of the Holy Name in Siddha Bakula. It was flooded with Rupa Goswami’s ecstasies of divine love. Mahaprabhu and all His associates set foot here. It should be in the hands of pure devotees who are in the line of Rupa Goswami. Pure Vaishnavas who go there and see the photos of Mayavadis and Kartabhajas on the wall and on the altar feel great pain. No servant of the servant of Lord Chaitanya can accept the insult to Hari Das Thakur’s place that comes from cowtowing to those who do not accept the eternity of the Holy Name, who imagine all kinds of meanings to the Holy Name (*artha-vāda*), and who ultimately try to establish the impersonal absolute, who merely make a show of practicing devotional service and of dressing like Vaishnavas, who try to put devotees and non-devotees on the same level, who call an ordinary jiva an avatar of the Supreme and thus commit an offense to Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. We draw the attention of the Siddha Bakula Math’s learned Mahant to this matter.”

It would appear that the deviations that were noted in the above criticism have been corrected, for according to the present mahant, Srinivas Das Goswami Mahant, the connection with the Vakreshwar line is accepted and orthodox Vaishnava doctrine and practice are followed.

## Chapter 26 - Hari Das Thakur Samadhi Math

Everyone who has read the Chaitanya Charitamrita is familiar with the account of Hari Das Thakur’s auspicious disappearance from this world:

One day, Mahaprabhu’s servant Govinda went to Hari Das’ cottage to give him prasad, as was his custom. When he arrived there, he saw that Hari Das was lying down and chanting the Holy Name very feebly. Govinda told him to sit up and take prasad, but Hari Das said, “I will go without eating today. I have not yet finished chanting my Holy Names, so how can I eat? Yet I cannot show disrespect to Lord Jagannath’s maha prasad.” So saying, he agreed to accept but a single morsel of the holy food.

The next day, Mahaprabhu Himself came to see Hari Das to ask him how he was. Hari Das paid his obeisances to the Lord and said, “My body is well, but my mind and intelligence are not.” The Lord asked, “What’s the matter?” Hari Das replied, “I can no longer maintain my vow of chanting three lakhs of names every day.” Out of affection for Hari Das, Mahaprabhu told him that there was no need for him to show such rigid attachment for the practice of devotional service in practice since he had already attained perfection. He advised him that he could thus reduce the number of Holy Names he chanted every day without incurring any fault.

With great humility, Hari Das then revealed what had really been bothering him: “Lord, I know that it will not be long before You end Your pastimes in this world. This has been bothering me for some time. I would not be able to stand living in this world without You, so please let me leave first. Let me give up my life with Your feet on my heart, my eyes fixed on Your face and my tongue uttering Your name, ‘Sri Krishna Chaitanya!’ Let my body drop in Your presence. This is my request. You are the compassionate Lord, so please fulfill my request.”

The Lord answered, “The all-merciful Lord Krishna will surely give you whatever you ask. But whatever pleasure I get in living comes from you. You are My companion; is it right for you to leave Me like this?”

Hari Das grabbed the Lord’s feet and said, “Don’t toy with me, O Lord. I am most unworthy, but please grant me this boon.” He continued very meekly –

*mora śiromaṇi kata kata mahāśaya*  
*tomāra līlārasahāya koṭi-bhakta haya*  
*āmā hena jadi eka kīṭa mari gela*  
*pipīlikā maile pṛthivīra kāṅhā hāni haila*  
*bhakata-vatsala tumi mui bhaktābhāsa*  
*avaśya pūribe prabhu mora ei āśa*

**“So many thousands of devotees participate in Your pastimes and all of them are my superiors. If a little insect like me should disappear, what difference will it make to You? Is the world affected by the death of a little ant? You are always kind to Your devotees, so please grant me this wish, even though I am only the shadow of a devotee.” (CC** [**3.11.40-42**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/11.40)**)**

The following morning, after visiting Lord Jagannath, Mahaprabhu came to Hari Das Thakur’s cottage with Svarupa Damodar, Raya Ramananda, Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya, Vakreshwar Pandit and many other associates. Hari Das paid his obeisances to all these devotees. Mahaprabhu then asked him how he was and Hari Das answered, “Everything is as You desire it.”

Mahaprabhu gave the order for kirtan to begin and His companions formed a circle around Hari Das. The Lord then began to glorify Hari Das unreservedly, to the wonderment of all the devotees each of who came, one by one, to bow before the Thakur and touch his holy feet. Krishna Das describes what followed –

*haridāsa nijāgrete prabhure basāilā*  
*nija-netra dui bhṛṅga mukha-padme dilā*  
*sva-hṛdaye āni dhari prabhura caraṇa*  
*sarva-bhakta pada-reṇu mastaka bhūṣaṇa*  
*śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu balen bāra bāra*  
*prabhu mukha mādhurī piye netre jala-dhāra*  
*śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya śabda karite uccāraṇa*  
*nāmera sahita prāṇa karila utkrāmaṇa*  
*mahā-yogeśvara prāya svacchande maraṇa*  
*bhīṣmera niryāṇa sabāra haila smaraṇa*

**Hari Das made Mahaprabhu sit down in front of him. The bees of his eyes alighted on the Lord’s lotus face. He took the Lord’s feet and placed them over his heart, and then took the dust of the devotees’ feet and sprinkled it on his head. Then, as the tears flowed from his eyes, he drank in the vision of the Lord’s face and repeated the words, “Sri Krishna Chaitanya Prabhu!” As he said these words, “Krishna Chaitanya,” he breathed his last, voluntarily leaving his body like a great yogi, reminding everyone of Bhishma. (CC** [**3.11.53-57**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/11.53)**)**

The devotees’ kirtan grew louder and louder, and the Lord lifted Hari Das’s body and started to dance ecstatically around the courtyard. Svarupa Damodar took control of the situation and had them make a pallet on which to place Hari Das’ remains. Krishna Das Kaviraj paints a vivid picture of the scene that followed:

The devotees placed Hari Das Thakur on the pallet and took him to the seashore in the midst of loud singing of the Holy Names. Mahaprabhu danced at the head of the procession, followed by Vakreshwar and the other devotees. They washed Hari Das’ body in the sea and the Lord said, “Now the sea has truly become a holy place.” Then He and the devotees drank the water that had washed Hari Das’ feet. They then smeared Hari Das’ body with Jagannath’s prasadi sandalwood pulp and dressed it with prasadi cloth and silk Rathayatra ropes. After this they dug a hole in the sand and laid him in it.

All around the devotees sang kirtan, while Vakreshwar danced ecstatically. Gauranga shoulted “Haribol, Haribol!!” and threw a handful of sand on Hari Das’ body. They made a pile of sand over the body and then covered the sandpile with a cloth. The kirtan continued, making a great tumultous noise that filled the sky. Then, after Mahaprabhu and the devotees had gone into the ocean and bathed, they circumambulated Hari Das’ samadhi amidst the sounds of the Holy Name. (CC [3.11.62-72](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/11.62))

Hari Das Thakur’s *tirodhāna-līlā* took place on the fourteenth day of the waxing moon in the month of Bhadra. The site where Mahaprabhu and His devotees buried him has been preserved to this day on the beach near the Swarga Dwar. Many important memorials and samadhis of great Gaudiya Vaishnavas such as Gopal Guru Goswami and his disciple Dhyana Chandra are also found in proximity to Hari Das Thakur’s samadhi.

The entire area around the Swarga Dwar was formerly the town’s cremation ground. There is a shrine to Hanuman named Shmashan Mahavira bearing testimony to the beach’s ancient vocation. Old accounts also say that the Vaishnava residence known as Sri Chaitanya Mandali was built near the cremation ground. As the town’s population grew and the area around the Swarga Dwar was inhabited, however, the cremation ground was moved a few hundred yards to the east.

Some people say that Vaishnavas used to practice their bhajan here precisely because it was a cremation ground, but it is not a Gaudiya Vaishnava custom to engage in practices of this sort, as do some Tantriks. If Vaishnavas came to live and worship in this area, it was because Mahaprabhu Himself had declared the to be area sanctified by the touch of Hari Das’ sacred body. Indeed, it was the proximity to Hari Das’ samadhi that resulted in the Satasan Math being built here, attracting many great Vaishnavas like Svarupa Das Babaji and Bhaktivinoda Thakur.

## Ownership controversies at the Math

Towards the end of the 19th century, different factions claimed proprietorship of the Samadhi Math, with the result that a long court case ensued. Many people at that time requested Bhaktivinoda Thakur to take over the management of the temple, but he was not eager to get entangled with those who saw holy sites such as this as nothing more than a piece of mundane property to be fought over. He thus built his place of worship a little distance from the Samadhi Math and only served it indirectly.

According to the sadhus at the Siddha Bakul Math, the two maths were once under united management, with disciples of Siddha Bakul Math serving as the Samadhi Math's mahants. The temple was thus originally in the hands of renounced Vaishnavas, who held that it was no one’s personal property. Later, however, the seva was given over to householders, the descendants of Mamu Thakur, ostensibly to place it on a more secure footing.

Eventually, the seva was inherited by Vraja Sundari Debya and Rami Debya, the daughters of Dayamayi Debya, who were also in possession of the Tota Gopinath temple. Unfortunately, Rami Debya’s son Kunja Bihari Deva Goswami did not follow the minimum standards of Vaishnava conduct and had furthermore fallen deeply into debt. He mortgaged his half of Tota Gopinath’s seva to the mahant of the Trimali Math, a Ramanujaite institution near the Sri Mandir, for Rs. 2,500. He also made an agreement in principle to sell the Hari Das Samadhi Math to a Punjabi developer, Karam Chand Singh, for which he received an advance payment of Rs. 5,000. The Punjabi developer’s intention was to tear down Hari Das’ samadhi and build a hotel and restaurant on the site.

With only a few days left before these debts became due, Charan Das Babaji’s disciple Ram Das Babaji intervened. With the assistance of his godsister Kumudini Shil, he paid off Kunja Bihari’s debts and purchased Hari Das Thakur’s samadhi from him.

However, matters did not stop there. Dayamayi Debya's will turning over proprietorship of the Tota Gopinath Math in its entirety to Kunja Bihari Goswami was challenged it in court by her other daughter, Vraja Sundari Debya, and her son, Gopinath Deva Goswami. Since the matter was before the courts when Kunja Bihari signed over the Hari Das' samadhi to Ram Das Babaji, they also challenged the legality of this agreement. When Gopinath Deva Goswami and his mother won the court decision, Ram Das went to them and begged them to allow him to continue running the temple. He promised to run it piously through donations and to maintain the highest standard of service. He was able to convince Vraja Sundari, and she signed a paper relinquishing any claim to the Samadhi Math.\[cxxx\]

An annual stipend of Rs. 50 used to come to the Samadhi Math from the royal coffers, but this was stopped when all these legal battles began. The Tota Gopinath temple’s adhikari, Padma Charan Dasji, claimed that this stipend should thenceforth be given over to the Gaura-Gadadhar deities established by Mamu Thakur in the Tota Gopinath Math. After fighting for this stipend for many years, he finally managed to win the favor of the royal house, but this victory was short-lived and the stipend was again stopped.

## The current temple

The temple currently standing on the site of the Hari Das Samadhi Math was built after Ram Das Babaji took over the seva. An unusual feature of the temple is the three figures of Gauranga, Nityananda and Advaita Prabhus, who are seated as if in meditation. The three Prabhus each have their own room and altar. Mahaprabhu occupies the central room, Nityananda is to His right, Advaita to His left. Carved in pillars on either side of the central door are figures of Jaya and Vijaya and Jagai and Madhai. Jagai-Madhai are, of course, the incarnations of Jaya-Vijaya in Gaura lila.

Usually the three Prabhus are conceived in dancing form. The only place where there is another such deity is the meditating Gauranga inside the Jagannath temple itself, in the northeast corner of the inner compound. This Gauranga deity was installed, it is said, by King Prataparudra himself.

The devotees at Hari Das Thakur’s samadhi say that the deities of the three Prabhus date from not long after Mahaprabhu’s disappearance. Many people refer to Hari Das’ Samadhi Math as “Bhajan Kuti.” They say that this is because after Hari Das’ disappearance, whenever Sri Chaitanya went for His bath in the sea, He would stop here to sit and chant the Holy Names for a while. He also continued bringing Jagannath’s maha prasad to Hari Das at his samadhi. The three seated deities are a reminder of this particular lila.

Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s poem (in box)

## On Hari Das’ Samadhi

**O! Born of Moslem parents, Hari Das!**  
**And trained in youth in Moslem creed,**  
**Thy noble heart to Vaishnava truth did pass! –**  
**Thy holy acts thy candour plead!**  
**Is there a soul that cannot learn from thee**  
**That man must give up sect for God?**  
**That thoughts of race and sect can ne’er agree**  
**With what they call Religion broad?**  
**Thy love of God and brother soul alone**  
**Bereft thyself of early friends, --**  
**Thy softer feelings oft to kindness prone**  
**Led on thyself for higher ends!!**  
**I weep to read that Kazees and their men**  
**Oft persecuted thee, alas!**  
**But thou didst nobly pray for th’ wicked then!**  
**For thou wert Vaishnava Hari Das!!**  
**And God is boundless grace to thee, O man!**  
**United thee to one who came**  
**To save the fallen souls from Evil’s plan**  
**Of taking human souls to shame.**  
**And he it was who led you all that came**  
**For life eternal, -- holy, -- pure!**  
**And gave you rest in Heaven’s enduring name**  
**And sacred blessings ever sure!**  
**Thy body rests upon the sacred sands**  
**Of Swarga Dwar near the seas,**  
**Oh! Hundreds come to thee from distant lands**  
**T’ enjoy a holy, thrilling glee!**  
**The waters roar and storming winds assail**  
**Thy ears in vain, Ah! Vaishnava soul!**  
**The charms of Vrindavan thy heart regale,**  
**Unknown the wheel of time doth roll!!**  
**He reasons ill who tells that Vaishnavas die**  
**When thou art living still in sound.**  
**The Vaishnavas die to live and living try**  
**To spread a holy life around!**  
**Now let the candid man that seeks to live**  
**Follow thy way on shores of time,**  
**Then posterity sure to him will give**  
**Like one song in simple rhyme.**

## Chapter 27 - Satasan Math

The Satasan Math is in the Swarga Dwar area, near Hari Das Thakur’s Samadhi Math. The words *sāt āsana* mean “seven seats.” Legend has it that the seven sages (Sapta Rishi) came to earth in order to worship Lord Jagannath here by the sea. One day, King Indradyumna came to take bath in the sea and saw the seven sages engaged in chanting the Holy Names aloud in this secluded place. He approached them and asked who they were, but they paid him no mind and simply continued chanting.

That night, Lord Jagannath appeared to Indradyumna in a dream. He instructed him to give the seven sages land where they could worship Him in tranquility. He also told Indradyumna to send them Lord Jagannath’s maha prasad every day. The king decided to give them land near the village of Jirakandi and sent them the deed. The sages refused the land, saying they had no need of worldly property. They did agree to accept the maha prasad, however, and so Indradyumna sent seven *āṭikās* of rice and seven *kaṛoās* of vegetable prasad every day.

The seven sages had no need of land, because they did not engage in deity worship. Later, when deities were installed in the Satasan Math, income from endowed lands became necessary to make the service possible. Thus the land in Jirakandi was later accepted. When the Satasan Math came under the aegis of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas, the seven seats took the names Boro Asan, Kadali Patka Asan, Giridhari Asan, Gopha Asan, Madan Mohan Deva Asan, Krishna Balaram Asan, and Shyamasundar Asan.

Regrettably, the place that was once home to some of Mahaprabhu’s leading associates, such as Jagadananda Pandit, Svarupa Damodar Goswami and Bhagavan Acharya, and up until recently to great saints like Svarupa Das Babaji, has now fallen on hard times. At one time, the Satasan Math was transformed into a place where immoral activities were permitted.

The Math had land holdings in Jirakandi and Kantikera villages, but the sevayats of the different Asans fought over them, with the result that they fell into debt. Another 68-acre block of land in Kathoari village was also fought over in the courts. Regular portions of maha prasad and stipends for the deity service given by the King of Puri’s office were stopped in all but the Madan Mohan Deva Asan.

When Siddhanta Saraswati was doing bhajan in the Giridhari Asan, he saw just how serious the situation had become in the Satasan Math. In order to reform the deity service there, he sought the support of many local Vaishnavas. Finally, Radha Damodar Das, Gadadhar Das, Govinda Das, Balaram Das and Krishna Charan Das signed a paper in 1901 turning the property over to Saraswati Thakur.

Unfortunately, some unscrupulous persons who were attached to illegitimate practices were threatened by Saraswati Thakur’s strict asceticism. They spread rumors about Saraswati and generally created a poisonous atmosphere, leading Bhaktivinoda Thakur to advise Saraswati to abandon the attempt to solve Satasan’s problems. In the course of time, all traces of devotional service were erased from the Satasan Math.

The situation deteriorated to the point that a certain Madhusudan Das, a renounced Vaishnava who was the disciple of Gauranga Das and sevaka at the Giridhari Asan, fell down and went so far as to sell the bricks of the temple building in order to pay off his debts.

Three of the asans, Boro Asan, Kadali Patka Asan and Gopha Asan no longer exist. Some outside persons have built their houses on the sites of these temples, which were originally located between the Giridhari Math and Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s Bhajan Kuti on the east side of Satasan Road.

## Sri Giridhari Asan

This is the site where Mahaprabhu’s associate Jagadananda Pandit lived and did his bhajan. It is right next door to Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s Bhakti Kuti. This temple formerly had a good collection of Vaishnava manuscripts.

In 1900, when Bhaktivinoda Thakur came to Puri, he was accompanied by Siddhanta Saraswati. Saraswati Thakur showed a deep desire to engage in bhajan by the seashore near Hari Das Thakur’s samadhi. Bhaktivinoda Thakur arranged with Puri’s sub-registrar, Jagabandhu Pattanayak, for him to be given the service of the Giridhari Asan of the Satasan Math.

Recently, Iskcon's Indradyumna Swami has been helping a lot with Giridhari Math. He has paid for many improvements there. Other Western devotees have also helped in other ways, most particularly a woman disciple of Bhaktivedanta Swami Maharaj from France named Saumya Dasi purchased a new deity of Radharani for Giridhari to replace one that had been stolen many years earlier.

The current Goswamis at the Giridhari Asana are Krishna Charan Das and Kashinath Panda. Fourteen samadhis of previous mahants are found on the property, including Vraja Kishor Das, Bhagavat Charan Das, Sanatan Das, Govinda Das, Nimai Charan Das, and Gauranga Das. The present day mahant seems not to belong to the same disciplic succession.

The deities worshiped here are Radha Giridhari (worshiped by Jagadananda Pandit), Radha Damodar (worshiped by Swarup Damodar Goswami), Jagannath, Baladeva, Subhadra and many Shalagrams.  
The Math is maintained by rents collected on nearby properties and by bhiksha.

## Madan Mohan Deva Asan

The deity of Madan Mohan is worshiped here. Some people say that Raghunath Das Goswami lived here and served this deity. Others say that he lived at the Giridhari Asan. Other deities on the altar include Srimati Radharani, Govindaji, Gopinath, Lalita, Nitai Gaura, Gopal, Lakshmi, Jagannath, Baladeva, Subhadra and about a dozen Salagrams.

Every month the Sri Mandir provides this temple with dahl, rice and ghee. For their  
other maintanence they perform bhiksha. It is in fair condition and the deities are being nicely worshiped according to a high standard.

The samadhis of ten previous mahants are found on the math premises:

1\) Jahnavi Goswami  
2\) Parameswar Das Goswami  
3\) Narayan Das Goswami  
4\) Pushpagati Das Goswami  
5\) Kamal Goswami  
6\) Kunja Bihari Das Goswami  
7\) Sadananda Das Goswami  
8\) Mohan Das Goswami  
9\) Narottam Das Goswami  
10\) Lakshman Das Goswami

The current mahant is named Srila Muralidhar Dasji Maharaj.

## Krishna Balaram Asan

This was Khanja Bhagavan Acharya’s place of bhajan. His Krishna Balaram deities are still worshiped here. Radha Krishna, Gopal and Lakshmi deities are also found on the altar.

Some of the Vaishnavas who served here in the past were Balaram Das, Gauranga Das, Raghunath Das, Ramananda Das, Shyama Charan Das, Gadadhar Das, Krishna Das. The current mahant is named Adhikari Acyutananda Das.  
This temple is very poor, its only maintenance coming from bhajan and bhiksha.

## Sri Shyamasundar Asan

The Shyamasundar Asan is just across from the Giridhari Math. The Radha Shyamasundar deities originally belonged to Mahaprabhu’s associate, Brahmananda Bharati. Nitai Gaura and a dozen or so Shalagrams are also present on the altar. The worship is currently under the control of the Goswamis at the Giridhari Asan.

Past sevaks were Madan Mohan Das, Ramachandra Das, Raghavendra Das, Nityananda Das, Radha Charan Das, Mohan Das, Kunja Bihari Das, Govinda Das.

An Orissan writer named Raghunath Baidya wrote a versified account of many significant places in the state. He also wrote a few things about the history of Satasan Math. According to him, the famous 18th century Bengali poet, Bharata Chandra Ray, spent time here as a Vaishnava studying the Gaudiya Vaishnava rasika literature. Afterwards, he returned to householder life and converted to Shaktaism. He eventually became the court poet of Raja Krishna Chandra of Nadia.

## Boro Asan

Deities of Radha Damodar were formerly worshiped here, but were later moved to Giridhari Asan. It is said that Svarupa Damodar Goswami used to do his bhajan at the Boro Asan. Some of the Vaishnavas who have served these deities over the years have been Gaura Charan Das, Vraja Kumar Das, Kunja Mohan Das, Radha Charan Das, Damodar Das, Radha Mohan Das, Krishna Charan Das and Janardan Das.

## Kadali Patka Asan

No deity was being worshiped at Kadali Patka Asan when Sundarananda wrote his *Śrī Kṣetra*. A famous siddha Vaishnava, Svarupa Das Babaji, lived here at the end of the 19th century. Bhaktivinoda Thakur met this Babaji during his first posting to Puri in the 1870’s. He wrote the following about him in his autobiography --

Svarupa Das Babaji was a great soul, a Vaishnava without peer. He would stay inside his cottage the whole day long, doing his bhajan. Then in the evening, he would come out and pay his prostrated obeisances to the holy Tulasi plant. Then he would loudly chant the Holy Names and sing, dance and cry in ecstasy. Vaishnavas would take this opportunity to visit him. Some of them would offer him small handfuls of Jagannath prasad. He would consent to accept only as much as he needed to satisfy his hunger and not more.

At this time, one of the Vaishnavas would read from Gaudiya Vaishnava scriptures like Chaitanya Bhagavata and he would listen. At ten o’clock, he would go back inside his cottage and again start his bhajan. He would go to the ocean while it was still dark, wash his hands and face and take a complete bath. He did this alone for fear that some Vaishnava would perform some service for him without his knowledge. He was blind in both eyes, so only Mahaprabhu knows how he managed to take his bath in the ocean all alone in the dark. There is no doubt that he was a siddha purush, a spiritually perfected soul. He had absolutely no material desires. In the evening I would sometimes go to take darshan of his lotus feet. He would talk with the people and his speech was very sweet. He instructed me to never forget the name of Krishna.\[cxxxi\]

It is also said that there was a highly-placed bureaucrat who would once in a while bring Svarupa Das maha prasad. The siddha mahatma said to this devotee, “You can bring me prasad on the first three days of the English month, but don’t bring me anything after that.” Svarupa Das’ reasoning was that at the beginning of the month, the bureaucrat would have just received his pay and so the money spent buying prasad would be sure to have come out of his honest wages. After that, the money would most likely have been earned illegally through bribes and kickbacks.

Svarupa Das Babaji’s samadhi is present on the Kadali Patka Asan grounds. Though the room where Svarupa Das lived and did his bhajan is still standing, it is not shown any special care by the present-day sadhus who live there, who use it for other purposes.

Sevakas at this asan over the years have been Yugala Kishor Das, Subal Charan Das, Bhagavata Das, Shyam Das, Manohar Das.

## Sri Gopha Asan

Gopha means cave or hole. In the past, some Vaishnavas would dig a small underground room to live in and do bhajan. Such an underground room was called a gopha or gupha. Some of the sadhus who served here were Rama Krishna Das, Sitaram Das, Haribandhu Das.

## Chapter 28 - Tota Gopinath Math

The gardens of the Yameshwar temple, or Yameshwar Tota, are in Gaurbat Sahi, in the southwestern corner of Puri town, to the south of the temple itself. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami made his residence here on the orders of Mahaprabhu Himself.

*gadādhara paṇḍita rahilā prabhura pāśe*  
*yameśvara prabhu jāṅre karāila ābāse*

**Gadadhar remained with Mahaprabhu in Jagannath Puri. The Lord arranged for him to live near the Yameshwar temple. (CC** [**2.15.183**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/15.183)**)**

The Lord would come to visit Gadadhar every single day in order to hear him speak on the Srimad Bhagavatam. The gardens here would remind Him of the flowered bowers around Radha Kund, while the sand dunes on the nearby beach made Him think of Govardhan. There was a large banyan tree in the garden that brought back memories of the eternal banyan in Vrindavan where Krishna played His flute to attract the gopis, and the sea itself made Him think of the Yamuna.

The Lord also often accepted Gadadhar Prabhu’s invitations to take prasad at Yameshwar Tota.

*jyaiṣṭha-māse prabhu yameśvara-ṭoṭā āilā*  
*bhakta-anurodhe tāṅhā bhikṣā je karilā*

**In the hot season, during the month of Jyestha, the Lord came to take His midday meal at Yameshwar Tota at the request of the devotees. (CC** [**3.4.116**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/4.116)**)**

Once, while the Lord was there, He sent for Sanatan Goswami to join Him. When Sanatan received the call, he immediately headed for Yameshwar by the shortest path – one that took him across the sand. The longer path – one that was shaded by buildings -- led through the town and past the Boro Deul. In his enthusiasm, Sanatan took the shorter route, resulting in his feet becoming blistered. When the Lord asked him why he had done so, Sanatan answered that he was afraid that the servants of Lord Jagannath would see or touch him, making them ritually impure and unfit to serve the Lord. For this reason he had avoided the road that took him near the temple. The Lord complimented Sanatan for observing Vaishnava etiquette so scrupulously.

## The Tota Gopinath deity

According to legend, the Gopinath deity that is worshiped at this math appeared in the following miraculous manner. Once, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu came to Yameshwar and was overcome with the ecstatic mood of separation. In this mood, He started scratching away at the sand, calling out, “Where is My Krishna? Where is the lord of My life?” Gadadhar Pandit saw Him and asked what He was doing.

The Lord answered mysteriously, “Gadadhar, if I find a buried treasure here, will you take care of it?” Gadadhar immediately answered, “I will take care of anything You give me with my very life.”

The Lord then said, “Look, My Lord’s crown is sticking out of the sand here. Touch it.” Gadadhar looked and saw that there was indeed a portion of carved black stone showing. He and some other devotees immediately dug around it and found that it belonged to the crown of a deity of Lord Krishna. Mahaprabhu told Gadadhar that this was Gopinath, and that he should serve this deity always, taking the banyan to be Vamshi Bata and the sea to be the Yamuna.

Vrindavan Das Thakur describes

*gadādhara bhavane mohana gopīnātha*  
*āchena je-hena nanda-kumāra sākṣāt*  
*āpane caitanya tāne kariyāchena kole*  
*atu pāṣaṇḍī-o se vigraha dekhi bhule*  
*dekhi śrī-muralī mukha aṅgera bhaṅgimā*  
*nityānanda ānanda-aśrura nahi sīmā*

**Krishna, the son of King Nanda, resided at Gadadhar’s house in His enchanting form as Gopinath. Lord Chaitanya personally embraced this deity, upon seeing which even an atheist would be transformed. When Nityananda Prabhu saw Gopinath with the flute touching His mouth, he shed limitless tears of sheer joy. (CC** [**2.7.114-6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/7.114)**)**

Sri Chaitanya’s disappearance\[cxxxii\]

According to some traditions, Mahaprabhu disappeared into the body of Tota Gopinath at the end of His pastimes in this world. Vasu Ghosh wrote, “I’ve lost my Gaurachand in Gopinath’s house.” According to one account, when it was time for Mahaprabhu to end His manifest pastimes, He entered Tota Gopinath’s altar. The curtains closed and Mahaprabhu entered the Deity. When the curtains opened, all that the devotees found was the flower garland that Mahaprabhu was wearing. In the kirtan mandap in front of Balaram’s altar, there is a small marble plaque on the floor with imprints of Krishna's lotus feet. This is said to be Mahaprabhu’s pushpa-samadhi. According to the temple devotees at Tota Gopinath, when Gadadhar Pandit left this world he entered the deity of Radharani.

Every year Lord Gaurasundar sent someone to Bengal to bring some reassuring message for his mother Sachi, the incarnation of motherly love. One year he sent Jagadananda Pandit, who not only took Mahaprabhu’s message, but on Paramananda Puri’s request, a piece of Mahaprabhu’s cloth and Jagannath’s maha prasad. While Jagadananda was in Bengal, he also visited Nabadwip and Shantipur before returning to Puri. This time, Advaita Prabhu gave a message in the form of a riddle for Mahaprabhu. The message was:

*bāulake kahiha loka ha-ila bāula*  
*bāulake kahiha hāṭe nā bikāya cāula*  
*bāulake kahiha kāje nāhika āula*  
*bāulake kahiha ihā kahiyāche bāula*

**Tell that crazy man everyone’s gone crazy.**  
**Tell that crazy man no one’s selling rice in the market.**  
**Tell that crazy man there’s no more use for crazies like him.**  
**Tell that crazy man that the crazy man said this.**  
**(CC** [**3.19.20-21**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/19.20)**)**

The word *bāula* means madman, while *āula* is a corruption of *ātura*, meaning distressed, suffering.\[cxxxiii\] Nobody could understand what Advaita Acharya meant by this riddle.\[cxxxiv\] Mahaprabhu understood that it meant that the purpose of his incarnation had been completed and so he simply said, “So be it.” In other words, he agreed to do as Advaita asked and wind up his pastimes in this world. This message was the beginning of the last chapter of Mahaprabhu’s incarnation. For so long he had been cultivating Radharani’s mood, now he lost himself in it completely.

The Lord’s divine madness began to grow stronger and stronger. One night he rubbed his cheek against the wall of the Gambhira, trying to get out to find Krishna. Svarupa Damodar and Ramananda would sing the songs of Chandi Das, Vidyapati and Jayadeva to try to bring him a little peace of mind, but on the whole, the last twelve years of Mahaprabhu’s life passed in this way with barely any difference between his waking and sleeping states.

Most of Mahaprabhu’s biographers—Murari Gupta, Kavi Karnapur, Vrindavan Das and Krishna Das Kaviraj—have written nothing about his disappearance. Only Lochan Das writes,

*tṛtīya prahara belā rabibāra dine*  
*jagannāthe līna prabhu hailā āpane*

**In the third watch on a Sunday, the Lord disappeared into Lord Jagannath’s body. (*****Caitanya-maṅgala*****)**

According to this account, Mahaprabhu embraced Lord Jagannath and disappeared into his body in the mid-afternoon on a Sunday, the Shukla Saptami of Asharh month, in the Gundicha temple.\[cxxxv\] Srivasa Pandit, Mukunda Datta, Govinda, Kashi Mishra, and others were present there. They saw Mahaprabhu go into the temple, but when they did not see him come out, they became anxious. They asked the pujari of the Gundicha temple to open the temple doors, but the pujari answered—

*guñjā-bāḍīra madhye prabhura haila adarśana*  
*sākṣāte dekhila gaura prabhura milana*  
*niścaya kariyā kahi śuna sarva jana*

**The Lord has disappeared inside the Gundicha temple. I saw Gaura enter into Jagannath with my own eyes, so I can tell you this with all certainty.** ***(Caitanya-maṅgala)***

Other than this, there are many other opinions on how Mahaprabhu disappeared, some of which are very old, others are more recent. Jayananda says the following in his *Caitanya-maṅgala:*

*nīlācale niśāe caitanya ṭoṭā grāme*  
*vaikuṇṭha yāite nivedila krame krame*  
*āṣāḍha saptamī tithi śuklā aṅgīkāra kari*  
*ratha pāṭhāiha yāba vaikuṇṭha purī*  
*āṣāḍha vañcita ratha vijayā nācite*  
*iṭala bājila vāma pāe ācambite*  
*caraṇe vedanā baḍa ṣaṣṭhīra divase*  
*se lakṣye ṭoṭāya śaraṇa avaśeṣe*  
*paṇḍita gosāñike kahila sarva kathā*  
*kāli daśa daṇḍa rātre caliba sarvathā*

**One night, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was in Tota Gopinath’s temple, when he announced that he intended to return to the spiritual world. “On the seventh day of the waxing fortnight, I wll return back to Vaikuntha after accompanying Jagannath’s cart to the Gundicha temple.” On the day of the Rathayatra, as the Lord was dancing, he struck his foot against a brick. The pain increased and on the Shashthi, it became quite terrible. For that reason, the devotees brought him to the Tota Gopinath temple and Mahaprabhu told Gadadhar Pandit that he intended to leave a few hours into the night.**

Dr. Biman Bihari Majumdar has commented on the above two accounts in the following way, “Although there is some difference in their accounts as far as the exact time of day, Jayananda and Lochan agree on the day and date. However, they do not agree on the exact place the Lord disappeared. The legend that Mahaprabhu died by drowning in the ocean is not reliable, as Dr. Dinesh Chandra Sen has clearly shown. If we accept that Mahaprabhu died a natural death, then it seems more probable that he would choose to spend his last moments with his friend Gadadhar at the Tota Gopinath temple.”\[cxxxvi\]

Other people say that Mahaprabhu left his body in the presence of his close friend Gadadhar Pandit, in a state of divine possession, and that his holy remains were buried on the grounds of the Tota Gopinath temple. Evidence for this can be found in the *Bhakti-ratnākara*, where where Narahari writes that when Narottam Das Thakur went to Jagannath Puri in the hope of meeting Lord Chaitanya, he was disappointed to arrive there too late, as Mahaprabhu had already wound up his visible pastimes. Narottam was overwhelmed with grief and went to see Gadadhar Pandit, but he had also disappeared. Gadadhar’s successor, Mamu Thakur, showed Narottam Mahaprabhu’s samadhi and said,

*ahe narottama ei khāne gaura hari*  
*nā jāni ki paṇḍite kahilā dhīri dhīri*  
*doṅhāra nayane dhārā bahe atiśaya*  
*tāhā nirakhite ebe pāṣāṇa hṛdaya*  
*nyāsī śiromaṇi ceṣṭā bujhe sadhya kāra*  
*akasmāt pṛthivī karilā andhakāra*  
*praveśilā ei gopīnāthera mandire*  
*hailā adarśana punaḥ nā āila bāhire*

**“O Narottam! I don’t know what our Lord Gaurahari whispered to Gadadhar Pandit Goswami on that day, but both of them started to cry so much. Even now my stone-like heart melts when I think of it. Who can understand the actions of Chaitanya, the chief of sannyasis? He suddenly plunged the world into darkness and entered into Gopinath’s temple, disappearing there forever—never to come out again.” (*****Bhakti-ratnākara*** **8.354-7)**

Many people want to equate Mahaprabhu’s disappearance with the death of an ordinary human being. To this end, they argue that when Mahaprabhu entered the Gundicha temple, the Pandas, who were jealous of his influence with the king, assassinated him and and buried his body somewhere on the temple grounds. Then, out of fear that the king would take action against them, they began to spread the rumor that Mahaprabhu had merged into Jagannath’s body. Another group suggests that since Mahaprabhu fell into the ocean many times in his ecstasies, it was very possible that on one occasion he actually did drwon and never returned.

All these different ideas leave the majority of people in confusion about what really happened to Mahaprabhu. In fact, Mahaprabhu continued to preach his doctrine of simultaneous oneness and difference (*acintya-bhedābheda*) even through his disappearance. Anyone to whom this truth has been revealed will be able to understand. Mahaprabhu is the Supreme Person. We, on the contrary, are insignificant jivas whose limited intelligence makes it impossible for us to understand the unlimited Lord unless the Lord himself rains down his mercy on us. Once the sun has set, we may use all the power stations in the world to generate an unlimited amount of electricity, but all this light will still not help us see it. We are obliged to wait for the sun to rise again if we wish to see it. In the same way, our own intelligence can never be sufficient to understand the Supreme Lord—we are entirely dependent on his mercy. Rather than becoming confused by such conflicting opinions, the ordinary jiva should profit from worshiping the Lord and thus learn the truth of his glories.

We know that some great devotees like Dhruva and avatars like Ramachandra ascended into the spiritual world in the very same body. What then is the reason for doubting that Mahaprabhu could have entered into either Jagannath’s body or that of Tota Gopinath?

For Gaudiya Vaishnavas, the words of the great Vaishnavas are accepted as equal to the revealed scriptures. Therefore, intelligent people will accept the version of the *Bhakti-ratnākara*, which cites Gadadhar Pandit’s successor at Tota Gopinath, Mamu Thakur, and *Caitanya-maṅgala*, both of which state that Mahaprabhu merged into the body of Tota Gopinath. This is the sign of intelligence, for both Narahari (the author of *Bhakti-ratnākara*) and Lochan Das are considered authorities for Gaudiya Vaishnavas.

## Gadadhar feeds Gaura-Nitai

One day Nityananda suddenly appeared at Yameshwar Tota while Gadadhar Prabhu was reading Srimad Bhagavatam in front of Gopinath. As soon as he was aware of Nityananda’s presence, Gadadhar stopped reading and got up to greet him. The two of them greeted each other with tears of love and other signs of divine ecstasy. The other devotees there surrounded them were affected by the ecstatic mood. Gopinath and Nityananda sat down together and began talking about Lord Chaitanya. After a few minutes, Gadadhar invited Nityananda to stay for dinner. Nityananda then presented Gadadhar with gifts for Gopinath -- a piece of colorful cloth and a big, 80-pound bag of fine Bengali rice.

Gadadhar prepared a humble meal, picking spinach from his garden and tamarind leaves, which he made into a paste, adding sea water to it for salt. He cooked Nityananda’s rice and made the offering to Gopinath. At that very instant, Lord Chaitanya suddenly appeared, the Maha Mantra on His lips, and began calling for Gadadhar. He said, laughing,

*hāsiyā balena prabhu kena gadādhara*  
*āmi ki nā hai nimantraṇa bhitara*  
*āmi to tomarā dui haite bhinna nai*  
*nā dile-o tomarā balete āmi lai*  
*nityānanda-dravya gopīnāthera prasāda*  
*tomāra randhana mora ithe āche bhoga*

**“What’s this, Gadadhar? Have I not been invited today? I am not distinct from the two of you, so even if you do not offer Me something, I will take it by force. Don’t you not think I would also like to enjoy a meal that combines Nityananda’s gifts, Gopinath’s prasad and your cooking?” (Cbh** [**3.7.142-6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/7.142)**)**

Mahaprabhu had been forcibly attracted by Gadadhar’s devotion and had so appeared, even though He had not been specifically invited on that day. The Lord continued to give profuse praise to Nityananda’s rice, Gopinath’s prasad and Gadadhar’s cooking.

## Mahaprabhu hears the Devadasi

Another time, Mahaprabhu was on His way to Yameshwar Tota when He heard a Devadasi singing a song from *Gīta-govinda* \[See box/page/formatted section\]

When Mahaprabhu heard the beautiful voice of the Devadasi, He was overwhelmed with love for Krishna, as if He were Radha responding to Krishna’s sadness and separation. Since the words were Krishna’s, He completely forgot that it was a woman singing. He ran toward the singer, thinking it was Krishna Himself. So absorbed was He in love that He ignored the thorny bushes and fences that blocked His path. And even after His body had been bloodied by the thorns, He paid His injuries no mind. He had no consciousness of anything other than Krishna.

Mahaprabhu’s servant, Govinda, knew that it was a Devadasi who was singing. He followed close behind the Lord, struggling to catch up as the Lord came closer to the singer. He called out, “Prabhu! It’s a woman singing!” and threw his arms around the Lord to stop Him.

As soon as the Lord heard the word “woman,” He immediately returned to external awareness. He turned away from the Devadasi and said,

*...govinda āji rākhilā jīvana*  
*strī-paraśa haile āmāra haito maraṇa*

**Govinda, you have saved My life! If I had touched a woman, it would have killed Me. (CC** [**3.13.85**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/13.85)**)**

On April 13, 1936, when Srila Prabhupada Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati came to visit the Tota Gopinath Math, he spoke on the Chaitanya Charitamrita, specifically on the time that Mahaprabhu heard the Devadasi singing the above song from *Gīta-govinda*. Prabhupada had Ananta Vasudeva Prabhu sing this song in the *gurjarī raga* in this very spot. All the devotees felt the overwhelming power of this kirtan.

*mām iyaṁ calitā vilokya vṛtaṁ vadhū-nicayena \|*

**She walked away when She saw Me in the midst of the thronging brides; and I, being an offender, was afraid and did nothing to stop Her. Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

*kiṁ kariṣyati kiṁ vadiṣyati sā ciraṁ viraheṇa \|*  
*kiṁ dhanena janena kiṁ mama jīvitena gṛheṇa \|\|2\|\|*  
*hari han hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva \|\| dhruva-padam \|\|*

**What will She do? And what will She say if We should stay apart too long? And if We are apart, what use to Me are wealth, friends, home or life itself? Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

*cintayāmi tad-ānanaṁ kuṭila-bhrū kopa-bhareṇa \|*  
*śoṇa-padmam ivopari bhramatākulaṁ bhramareṇa \|\|3\|\|*  
*hari han hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva \|\| dhruva-padam \|\|*

**I recall Radha’s face, Her brow bent with the weight of anger, looking like a red lotus tormented by a hovering bumblebee. Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

*tām ahaṁ hṛdi saṅgatām aniśaṁ bhṛśaṁ ramayāmi \|*  
*kiṁ vane'nusarāmi tām iha kiṁ vṛthā vilapāmi \|\|4\|\|*  
*hari han hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva \|\| dhruva-padam \|\|*

**She is with Me in My heart where We make passionate, unending love. Should I look for Her in the woods? Ah, why am I wasting time here, prattling? Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

*tanvi khinnam asūyayā hṛdayaṁ tavākalayāmi \|*  
*tan na vedmi kuto gatāsi na tena te'nunayāmi \|\|5\|\|*  
*hari han hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva \|\| dhruva-padam \|\|*

**O slender one! I know now that Your heart is weary with jealousy. But I don’t know where to find You, so how can I beg for Your forgiveness? Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

*dṛśyase purato gatāgatam eva me vidadhāsi \|*  
*kiṁ pureva sasambhramaṁ parirambhaṇaṁ na dadāsi \|\|6\|\|*  
*hari han hatādaratayā gatā sā kupiteva \|\| dhruva-padam \|\|*

**You appear before Me and make Me run around trying to catch You, why do You not give Me the excited embraces You once did? Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

**Forgive me, Radhe! Never again will I do anything like this. My beauty, show yourself to Me, for I am being tortured by the god of love. Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

**The humble, yet talented Jayadeva, the moon born from the ocean of Kendubilva, describes this picture of the love-blind Madhusudana. Lord! Lord! My Radha has left Me, angered by My insensitivity to Her love.**

## Vallabhacharya and Gadadhar Pandit

The scholar Vallabha Bhatta once came to Yameshwar Tota to seek Gadadhar Pandit’s help in getting an audience with Mahaprabhu. He had written a commentary on the holy names of Krishna that he wished to read to the Lord, but Mahaprabhu’s devotees had not shown much interest in this text. Knowing of Gadadhar’s close friendship with the Lord, he came to see him to ask if he would listen to a reading of this work. Gadadhar said to him,

*antaryāmī prabhu jānibena mora mana*  
*tāṅre bhaya nāhi kichu viṣama tāṅra gaṇa*

**The Lord resides inside us all, so He will know what I am thinking. Therefore I do not fear Him. But His associates are very critical. (CC** [**3.7.98**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/7.98)**)**

Vallabha Bhatta worshiped the child Krishna with the Bal Gopal mantra in the mood of parental love. The association of Gadadhar Pandit changed him, however, and he was attracted to worshiping Krishna in His form as a charming youth. With this change, he began to ask Gadadhar repeatedly to give him the appropriate mantras and instruction for this kind of worship. Gadadhar had some reservations and so he refused, saying, “I cannot be your spiritual master. I am subservient to my master, Gaurasundar. Without His permission, I can do nothing. The Lord thinks poorly of me because I allow you come here to see me.” (CC [3.7.149-152](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/7.149))

A few days later, however, Mahaprabhu changed his attitude to Vallabha Bhatta. Mahaprabhu is the supreme potent, whereas Gadadhar Pandit is His potency. Therefore, devotees call Mahaprabhu “Gadadhara-Prananath” and “Gadaier Gauranga,” indicated the special character of their relationship. Thus, a few days later, when Gadadhar invited Mahaprabhu and His associates for lunch, Vallabha Bhatta also came with them. This time Vallabha had Mahaprabhu’s permission to take initiation from Gadadhar Pandit.

## King Vibhishan and the Poor Brahmin

The last pastime described in Lochan Das’ Chaitanya Mangal\[cxxxvii\] takes place in the Tota Gopinath temple.

There was once a poor South Indian Brahmin named Rama. He was so poverty-stricken that he was near starvation. He realized that his misery was the result of his past sins, but he did not know how he could be freed from his sufferings. He heard that the lord of the universe, Lord Jagannath, could help him, so he set off on pilgrimage to Purushottam Kshetra to beg the Lord for His mercy.

When in Puri, the Brahmin came every day to take darshan of the lotus-eyed Lord, praying for relief from his poverty-stricken condition and asking to be given wealth. He begged a little Maha Prasad and then returned, threatening to kill himself if Lord Jagannath did not give him abundant riches. He then started to fast.

While this was going on, Mahaprabhu was at the Tota Gopinath temple, sitting in the company of His intimate devotees, enjoying discussions of the glories of Vrindavan. He became affected by the Brahmin’s prayers, however, and suddenly fell silent.

The Brahmin fasted for seven days, but without any result. Finally he decided to drown himself in the ocean. He went to the Swarga Dwar, but as he prepared to throw himself under the waves, a huge figure, as tall as a mountain, suddenly emerged from the water. The man walked ashore and assumed the size of an ordinary man, astonishing the Brahmin and making him think that it must be Lord Jagannath Himself.

The mysterious man asked the Brahmin who he was and what he was doing. The Brahmin said, “I am suffering because of my extreme poverty. I can't maintain my brahminical status. I pass my days and nights without eating anything. My family doesn't care for me. I have no shelter. I prefer death to life, so I have decided to commit suicide by starvation.”

The man introduced himself as Vibhishan, and told the Brahmin that he was going to see Lord Jagannath, but instead of going to the Jagannath temple, he took the Brahmin to Tota Gopinath, where Mahaprabhu was sitting with Paramananda Puri, Govinda, and some other associates. Mahaprabhu invited the two Brahmins in, and engaged in an affectionate conversation with Vibhishan, as though they were old friends who were seeing each other after a long time. This mystified the other devotees, none of who recognized Vibhishan. The South Indian Brahmin, meanwhile, stood shyly behind the other devotees.

Lord Chaitanya said to the Brahmin sitting beside him, “This Brahmin standing in the back is suffering terribly. He has lost all his wisdom due to poverty and so has come here to blame Lord Jagannath for his difficulties and harass Him for money.”

Mahaprabhu went on: “It is human nature to never find fault with oneself. People commit sin, but blame the Lord when they suffer as a result. And when they are happy, they think it is their own merit. This man has foolishly been seeking death by fasting for the last seven days. But what can Lord Jagannath do for him? He has had the good luck to see you, for you can give him the wealth he desires and make him happy."

Vibhishan agreed to do as ordered by the Lord and then left with Rama, starting back to the ocean. The poor Brahmin was filled with questions, but above all he wanted to know why they had not gone to see Lord Jagannath. Vibhishan chastised him, saying, "You dull-headed fool! You just saw Lord Jagannath in person. Your desire for wealth has been fulfilled by His mercy. Now let’s be off to your home where I will give you the money you want so badly."

The Brahmin began to hit his head in anguish and asked to be taken back to see Mahaprabhu again. The Brahmin came before the Lord and said, “O Lord, I am an ignorant fool. You are the life and soul of innumerable living entities. You are Lord Jagannath Himself. Due to my bad karma, I suffered from poverty, disease and other miseries. I came to You and asked to be cured of my poverty, but I did not understand what was the true medicine for my disease. Please give me what I need to be cured of the suffering of material life.”

Mahaprabhu laughed and said, “Lord Jagannath did you a favor. Now go on accepting the results of your work as you deserve, whether it is happiness or distress. In the end, you will attain Lord Jagannath’s lotus feet.”

When all the devotees came to understand what had happened, they exploded with love for the Lord, and shouted “Haribol! Haribol!” in ecstatic love.

## Mamu Thakur

Gadadhar Pandit’s successor in charge of the Tota Gopinath temple was Mamu Thakur, who came from the village of Magdoba in Faridpur district. His real name was Jagannath Chakravarti. He was the nephew of Nilambara Chakravarti, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's maternal grandfather, thus related to Mahaprabhu as His maternal uncle. In Orissa, the maternal uncle is called *māmū,* thus Jagannath Chakravarti was known popularly as Mamu Thakur.

There is a legend that when Mamu Thakur became very old while serving Tota Gopinath. His back became so curved that he could not reach the deity’s head to place a flower garland on it. The Thakur became depressed at seeing this difficulty in serving the Lord and asked the Lord to let him die. Instead of fulfilling this wish, however, Gopinath changed his form, shortening His legs so that Mamu Thakur could reach his head. Some people say that Gopinath is sitting in the lotus position, but in fact, His feet are shorter. This is the form in which Gopinath can be seen to this day. This story of the Lord’s kindness to His devotee so appealed to a poet from Southern India that he wrote a play in Sanskrit about it. The play has now been lost, but the following charming verse remains --

*ābālyād bhūṣayaṁs tvāṁ sukham aham anayaṁ vatsarāṇām aśītiṁ*  
*nādya sthāne samarthas tava śirasi vibho mallikā-dāma dātum \|*  
*tenāyur me yathedaṁ na bhavati ca vṛthā tac ca svāmin vidheyaṁ*  
*bhaktenoktaṁ pragṛhṇaṁs tad-avadhi bhagavān bhakta-bandhur niviṣṭaḥ \|\|*

**“I have served You, O Lord, since I was a tiny child, and since then, I have dedicated more than eighty years to Your service. Now I can no longer stand up straight to place this garland of jasmine flowers on Your head. Now, my Lord, please act in such a way that my life does not become completely useless. You are the friend of the devotees, for You always accept the request of Your devotee.”**

Some recount the same story in a slightly different way. They say that at the end of his life Gadadhar Pandit was suffering so much from separation of Mahaprabhu that he aged very quickly. In his old condition he could not reach Tota Gopinath's head to put a crown on Him, hence the Lord sat down in order to accommodate him.

Another reason is given for Gopinath’s being seated in the lotus posture. In the description of the rasa dance in the Bhagavatam, the following verse is found –

*tatropaviṣṭo bha gavān sa īśvaro*  
*yogeśvarāntar-hṛdi kalpitāsanaḥ*  
*cakāsa gopī-pariṣad-gato 'rcitas*  
*trailokya-lakṣmy-eka-padaṁ vapur dadhat*

**The Lord, who is meditated on by the yogis as seated in their hearts, sat there in the midst of the gopis, His form appearing like the repository of all the beauty in the three worlds.**

Sometime after Gopinath changed form in this way, He was joined by Radharani and Lalita who stand to His either side. These deities are unique in that they are both black. The mahants of the math give the following reason for their having this color: When Krishna took the form of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, He took on the color and mood of Srimati Radharani. However, Radha also becomes so absorbed in Krishna that She takes on His mood and color. Similarly, Lalita Devi, who was Svarupa Damodar in Mahaprabhu’s lila, played the role of Krishna in order to bring the Lord pleasure. So the Lalita deity in Gopinath’s temple holds a flute and stands in the threefold bending form, just as Krishna did when calling the gopis to the woods by the banks of the Yamuna. Some people say that this is not Lalita Devi, but Ananga Manjari.

In fact, many old Radharani deities in Orissa are black. Kanai Kuntia's Radharani, the consort of Vrindavan Chandra, is made of black stone like Radha and Lalita at Tota Gopinath. Several hundred years ago it was common to make both Radha and Krishna Deities from black stone because this particular kind of stone is very resilient.  
There is another temple room to the south of Gopinath, where Balaram is accompanied by Revati and Varuni. To the north is another temple room where deities consecrated by Mamu Thakur are present. These are Gaura-Gadadhar and Radha-Madan Mohan. There is also a shrine to Gopishwar Mahadeva. This Shiva deity is given full rice offerings every day.

## Gadadhar Pandit’s successors

The devotees at Tota Gopinath Math give their disciplic succession as follows

1\. Gadadhar Pandit (Srimati Radharani or Saubhagya Manjari)  
2\. Mamu Thakur (Sri Rupa Manjari)  
3\. Raghunath Goswami  
4\. Ramachandra Deva Goswami  
5\. Radha Vallabha Deva Goswami  
6\. Krishna Jivan Deva Goswami  
7\. Shyamasundar Deva Goswami  
8\. Shantamani Deva Goswami  
9\. Harinath Deva Goswami  
10\. Navinachandra Deva Goswami  
11\. Matilal Deva Goswami  
12\. Dayamayi Debya  
13\. Kunja Bihari Deva Goswami  
14\. Ranganath Deva Goswami  
15\. (current mahant)

Tota Gopinath had no land holdings when Gadadhar Pandit was His servant. King Prataparudra tried to make a large gift of land to facilitate His service, but Gadadhar refused, saying that as he was a renunciate, he could not accept gifts from royalty. He made it his vow to live on madhukari, and to serve Gopinath with what he collected in this way. Mamu Thakur followed the example given by Gadadhar Pandit, but subsequently, this ideal of behavior was relaxed. Gopinath’s properties were near Puri town, in the area of Mangala Ghat, west of the town.

Special festivals held in the Tota Gopinath temple are Baladeva’s appearance day, Krishna Janmashtami, Nandotsava, Radhashtami, Govardhana Puja, Gadadhar Pandit’s disappearance day (Asharh Amavasya), and Dol Purnima. On Gadadhar Pandit's disappearance day, Tota Gopinath is dressed in Sad-bhuja Vesh. In Karttik, special lower legs and feet are attached Tota Gopinath so that all of the pilgrims can see His lotus feet.

The famous siddha Vaishnava Tin Kori Goswami did bhajan for many years just behind the Tota Gopinath temple. Tin Kori Prabhu not only wore a dress of burlap bags, but also used burlap as mosquito netting. He would daily chant three lakhs and in the late afternoon speak a little katha to the devotees who came to see him. On Ekadasis he would chant all night and since he was not sleeping he would not use his makeshift mosquito netting.

Bhakti Promode Puri Maharaj wrote in 1968, after a visit to the Tota Gopinath temple:

His Holiness Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj took sannyas here in the Tota Gopinath grounds. We sat on the very veranda where the fire sacrifice had been performed on that occasion and drank water from Pandit Goswami’s well. Srila Acharya Deva asked Hrishikesh Maharaj to sing the prayers to Gopinath from Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s *Kalyāṇa-kalpa-taru.*

## GOPINATH

*gopīnātha, mama nivedana śuno*  
*viṣayī durjana, sadā kāma-rata*  
*kichu nāhi mora guṇa*

**O Gopinath, Lord of the Gopis, please hear my request! I am suffering from my attachments, always addicted to worldly desires, and devoid of good qualities.**

*gopīnātha, āmāra bharasā tumi*  
*tomāra caraṇe, loinu śaraṇa,*  
*tomāra kiṅkara āmi*

**O Gopinath, You are my only hope I have taken shelter at your lotus feet as your eternal servant.**

*gopīnātha, kemone śodhibe more*  
*na jāni bhakati, karme jaṛa-mati*  
*poṛechi saṁsāra-ghore*

**O Gopinath, how will you purify me? I do not know what devotion is, my mind is burdened with greed, and I have fallen into a perilous darkness.**

*gopīnātha, sakali tomāra māyā*  
*nāhi mama bala, jñāna sunirmala*  
*swādhīna nahe e kāyā*

**O Gopinath, I am surrounded by illusions. I have no strength or understanding, and I am far from being liberated from earthly temptations.**

*gopīnātha, niyata caraṇe sthāna*  
*māge e pāmara, kāṇḍiyā kāṇḍiyā,*  
*korohe karuṇā dāna*

**O Gopinath, an eternal place at Your divine feet is what I beg for, weeping and weeping, please give me the gift of Your mercy.**

*gopīnātha, tumi to sakali pāro*  
*durjane tārite, tomāra śakati,*  
*ke āche pāpīra āro*

**O Gopinath, You are able to do anything, and You have the power to deliver us all. Who could be more lost than myself?**

*gopīnātha, tumi kṛpa-pārābāra*  
*jīvera kāraṇe, āsiyā prapañce,*  
*līlā koile subistāra*

**O Gopinath, You are the ocean of mercy. Having come into this phenomenal world for the sake of the fallen souls, You expand Your divine pastimes.**

*gopīnātha, āmi ki doṣe doṣī*  
*asura sakala, pāilo caraṇa,*  
*vinoda thākilo bosi*

**O Gopinath, what sin has made me so sinful that although all the demons attained your lotus feet, Bhaktivinoda has remained here in worldly existence.**

## Chapter 29 - Jagannath Vallabha Math

## History

The Jagannath Vallabha Math is situated about halfway between the Jagannath and Gundicha temples. It is in the Jagannath Vallabha garden, a 2&frac12; hectare block of land, filled with coconut trees, mango orchards and flower gardens, bordered to the east by the Boro Danda, the south by Chudanga Sahi, the west by Markandeshwar Sahi and to the north by Narendra Sarovar. The word *vallabha* means “beloved,” and this garden is truly dear to Lord Jagannath. It has supposedly been in existence as long as the Jagannath temple itself. It supplies flowers and fruits for Lord Jagannath’s puja and offerings every day.

No one has been able to establish beyond any doubt who founded the math that stands within these gardens, or when it was done. According to some traditions, this was the original headquarters of the Vishnuswami sampradaya. Some say that Ramananda Raya’s family guru belonged to the Vishnuswami line, explaining why Ramananda spent so much time in the Jagannath Vallabha gardens.

Up until about 130 years ago, renounced Vaishnava monks lived at the Math and took care of the deities. The then mahant embezzled about ten thousand rupees – a sizable sum in those days -- from the temple’s treasury and left, ostensibly to go on pilgrimage. Instead, he returned to his home village and got married. Hired Brahmins kept the service going for some time, but in 1863, the British passed an act that placed the math under the management of a committee headed by the Cuttack district judge. In 1939, the British passed the Orissan Hindu Religious Endowments Act, through which a three-man trust board was created under the jurisdiction of the Endowments Commissioner. This situation obtains to this day, so the math has no mahant.

The temple building at the Jagannath Vallabha Math faces the east. The middle room of the temple has a four-armed form of Krishna known as Radha Gopal. He holds a flute in two of His four hands, a discus in his other right hand and a conch in the left. In the room to the right are deities of Jagannath, Balaram, Subhadra and Sudarshan. On September 24, 1944, Adikanda Das Babaji organized the installation of deities of Raya Ramananda and Lord Chaitanya in sannyasi vesh. The consecration ritual was performed by Pandit Narasingha Mishra. These deities are served in a separate building to the right of the entrance of the Jagannath Vallabha Math temple compound.

Besides the math, there are a number of other shrines dedicated to Hanuman and the Goddess in the garden. Hanuman is present in the forms of Boro Mahabir, Gumpha Mahabir and Supari Bari Mahabir. Devi is present as Anjana Devi and Buri Thakurani. Gumpha Mahabir is also known by the name Suranga Mahabir. Suranga means “tunnel” and this name is a reminder that at one time there was an underground passage that linked the Jagannath Vallabha gardens to the Boro Deul or main temple of Jagannath.

## Mahaprabhu’s lila

This beautiful garden has long brought pleasure to the Lord and His devotees. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu often visited these gardens, especially during the nine days of the Rathayatra festival when the Lord was in the Gundicha temple.

*jagannātha-vallabha nāma baṛa puṣpārāma*  
*nava dina karena prabhu tāhāte viśrāma*

**Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu would come to the Jagannath Vallabha gardens to rest every day during the nine-day Rathayatra festival period. (CC** [**2.14.105**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/14.105)**)**

In His later pastimes, Mahaprabhu would be absorbed in the mood of the chief gopi, Srimati Radharani, displaying all the symptoms of her Maha Bhava. Krishna Das Kaviraj has described a pastime where, near the end of His sojourn on this earth, Mahaprabhu had a vision of Krishna in Jagannath Vallabha gardens:

*eka-kāle vaiśākhera paurṇamāsī-dine*  
*rātri-kāle mahāprabhu calilā udyāne*  
*jagannātha-vallabha nāma udyāna-pradhāne*  
*praveśa karilā prabhu lañā bhakta-gaṇe*  
*praphullita vṛkṣa-vallī jena vṛndāvana*  
*śuka śārī pika, bhṛṅga kare ālāpana*  
*puṣpa-gandha lañā bahe malaya-pavana*  
*guru hañā taru-latāya śikhāya nācana*  
*pūrṇa-candra-candrikāya parama ujjvala*  
*taru-latādi jyotsnāya kare jhalamala*  
*chaya ṛtu-gaṇa jāhāṅ vasanta pradhāna*  
*dekhi ānandita hailā gaura bhagavān*

**Once, on a full-moon night in the month of Vaishakh, Lord Chaitanya Mahaprabhu went with His devotees to the principal garden in Jagannath Puri, known as Jagannath Vallabha.**  
**As it was summer, the trees and creepers in the garden were fully blossomed, and the bumblebees, the mynahs, parrots and koyils sang sweet melodies, reminding the Lord of Vrindavan. Mild breezes wafted from the south, carrying the fragrance of flowers. Playing the role of a teacher, the breeze taught the trees and creepers how to dance. Everything was illuminated by the full moon and the garden foliage glittered in the silver light. All six seasons, especially spring, seemed present there. Seeing the beauty of the garden, the Supreme Lord Gauranga was overjoyed.**

*lalita-lavaṅga-latā pada gāoāñā*  
*nṛtya kari bulena prabhu nija-gaṇa lañā*  
*prati-vṛkṣa-vallī aiche bhramite bhramite*  
*aśokera tale kṛṣṇe dekhena ācambite*

**In this atmosphere, the Lord had His associates sing a verse from the** ***Gīta-govinda*****, beginning with the words** ***lalita-lavaṅga-latā*** **\[SEE BOX\], while He danced and wandered about with them. As He thus wandered around every tree and creeper, He suddenly saw Lord Krishna beneath an ashoka tree.**

*kṛṣṇa dekhi mahāprabhu dhāñā calilā*  
*āge dekhi hāsi kṛṣṇa antardhāna ha-ilā*  
*āge pāilā kṛṣṇe tāṅre punaḥ hārāñā*  
*bhūmete paṛilā prabhu mūrcchita hañā*  
*kṛṣṇera śrī-aṅga-gandhe bhariche udyāne*  
*sei gandha pāñā prabhu hailā acetane*  
*nirantara nāsāya paśe kṛṣṇa-parimala*  
*gandha āsvādite prabhu ha-ilā pāgala*

**When Mahaprabhu saw Krishna, He began running very swiftly toward Him, but Krishna simply smiled and disappeared. Mahaprabhu was devastated at losing Krishna after having found Him and fell into a swoon. The entire garden was filled with the scent of Lord Krishna's transcendental body, upon smelling which the Lord at once fell unconscious. But as this scent continued to enter His nostrils, the Lord became mad to relish it. (CC** [**3.19.78-89**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-antya/19.78)**)**

*ei-mata gaurahari, gandhe kaila mana-curi,*  
*bhṛṅga-prāya iti-uti dhāya*  
*jāya vṛkṣa-latā-pāśe, kṛṣṇa sphure----sei āśe,*  
*kṛṣṇa nā pāya, gandha-mātra pāya*  
*svarūpa-rāmānanda gāya, prabhu nāce sukha pāya,*  
*ei-mate prātaḥ-kāla haila*  
*svarūpa-rāmānanda-rāya, kari nānā upāya,*  
*mahāprabhura bāhya-sphūrti kaila*

**Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, His mind lost to that scent, ran back and forth like a bumblebee greedy for honey. He ran to the trees and plants, hoping that Lord Krishna would reappear, but all He found was this maddening fragrance.**  
**Even so, the Lord found joy in dancing through the night while Svarupa Damodar and Ramananda Raya sang to Him. When morning came, these two companions devised a plan to bring Him back to external consciousness. (CC 3.19.99-100)**

## SONG 3 from Gīta-govinda.

*lalita-lavaṅga-latā-pariśīlana-komala-malaya-samīre \|*  
*madhukara-nikara-karambita-kokila-kūjita-kuñja-kuṭīre \|\|1\|\|*

Ramananda Raya composed a play, which he named *Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka*. This short play is a romantic comedy about Radha and Krishna’s *pūrva-rāga* and culminates with the Divine Couple’s union. In many ways it is modeled after the *Gīta-govinda,* containing a number of songs.

Ramananda taught this play to two Devadasis who were to perform it for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord and King Prataparudra. Two verses from this play have been quoted in the Chaitanya Charitamrita, both of them spoken by Radharani --

*prema-ccheda-rujo 'vagacchati harir nāyaṁ na ca prema vā*  
*sthānāsthānam avaiti nāpi madano jānāti no durbalāḥ*

*dvi-trāṇy eva dināni yauvanam idaṁ hā-hā vidhe kā gatiḥ*

**This Krishna does not understand how we suffer from the disease of interrupted love; nor does love, which has no knowledge of who is an appropriate object, and who not; nor does Cupid, who knows however how weak we are. Nobody really knows in the least the sufferings of another! Our lives are not under our control, Our youth and beauty will last only two or three days more – Oh God! What will become of us then?**

*yadā yāto daivān madhu-ripur asau locana-pathaṁ*  
*tadāsmākaṁ ceto madana-hatakenāhṛtam abhūt*  
*punar yasminn eṣa kṣaṇam api dṛśor eti padavīṁ*  
*vidhāsyāmas tasminn akhila-ghaṭikā ratna-khacitāḥ*

**When Fate deemed that the enemy of Mura should cross the path of my vision, my heart was stolen away by that wretch Cupid. If He should ever come before my eyes again, then I shall worship ever nanosecond of that moment by ornamenting them with jewels.**

## Service and Festivals

The Jagannath Vallabha garden still provides flowers for many of Lord Jagannath’s decorations, like tilak and jhumpa for Boro Sringar Vesh every evening. The math supplies kora, a sweet made of coconut, for the Kaliya Daman and Pralambasura vadh Veshas on the Ekadasi and Dvadasi following Janmashtami.

There are also some special festivals that take place in this garden –

**(1) Damanaka Yatra**

Every Chaitra Shukla Trayodasi, the deities of Rama and Krishna are taken in procession to the Jagannath Vallabha Math in order to steal damanaka (or dayna) bushes. On first arriving in the garden, Rama and Krishna are taken to the Jhulan Mandap, where they are given Gandharva Puja and bhoga. Then, without any fanfare, the temple servants carry the two deities into the garden to silently steal the flower shrubs. In all, about twelve of these flower bushes, which have been prepared the previous day, are uprooted and given to the two deities who then return to the temple. These bushes are offered to Lord Jagannath, Lady Subhadra and Lord Balarama on the following day.

**(2) Vasanta Panchami**

On this day, Dol Govinda, Lakshmi, and Saraswati are taken to the Jhulan Mandap in the Gardens where they are offered colored powders, sandalwood, betelnut, and bhoga. After they have been worshiped in this way, they are taken back to the main temple.

**(3) Fortnightly events**

Every fortnight, from Dasami to Trayodasi, Dol Govinda, Lakshmi, and Saraswati are taken to a place on the Boro Danda in front of the Jagannath Vallabha gardens.
