They are offered panti bhoga (food offerings made at a distance), which is placed on the temple veranda. Colored powders, sandalwood and betelnut are also offered before the deities are returned to the temple.

**(4) Bent Yatra**

This festival takes place in the month of Phalgun. Bent (*beṇṭa*) means “hunt” in Orissan, and this festival is a reenactment of Lord Ramachandra and Lakshman’s hunting activities during while banished to the forest. The Rama and Lakshman deities are taken from their shrine in the main temple compound to the Bent Pukur, a small pond in the Jagannath Vallabha garden where twelve green coconuts have been placed. The sevayats touch a bow and arrows to Rama and Lakshman’s hands and then shoot at the coconuts.

**(5) Dugdha Melani Yatra**

Two days prior to the Orissan new year’s day on Makara Sankranti, the Rama and Krishna deities are taken to a temporary shelter set up on the Boro Danda in front of the garden. One of the cows kept in the garden is brought to the deities and tied up near them. A servant of the Mahabhoi category milks the cow and this raw milk is then offered to Rama and Krishna. Afterward, the deities are taken back to the temple.

**(6) Rama Navami**

For the seven days following Rama Navami, the three deities of Rama, Lakshman and Sita Devi are brought to the garden where Rama Lila is put on by special servants. Special offerings of panti bhoga are made.

## Bhaktivinoda Thakur at Jagannath Vallabha Math

While Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur was in Puri between 1870 and 1874, he founded a regular group for discussion of the Bhagavata, Bhagavata Samsad, which was held at the Jagannath Vallabha Math. Many of the leading Vaishnavas in Puri such as Nityananda Das, Paramananda Das, Narayan Das Mahant, Harihar Das Mahant of Uttara Parshwa Math were attracted to hearing the Bhagavatam from his lips. He also listened to the discourses of Sri Gopinath Pandit.

A certain renounced Vaishnava, Raghunath Das Babaji of Hati Akhra, objected to the Thakur’s speaking on Bhagavatam because he had not been initiated and wore neither tilak nor tulasi mala. Shortly thereafter, Raghunath Das was afflicted by a serious illness. Lord Jagannath appeared to him in a dream and ordered him to beg Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur for forgiveness, after doing which he was cured.\[cxxxviii\]

## Chapter 30 - Other Gaudiya Vaishnava Maths

## Sri Puri Goswami Math

This math is situated on the Lokanath Road in the neighborhood known as Baseli Sahi, not far to the west of the Jagannath temple, just next to the police station. It was here that Mahaprabhu’s associate Paramananda Puri lived.

*eka dina prabhu purī gosāṇira maṭhe*  
*basilena giyā tāna parama-nikaṭe*  
*paramānanda purīre prabhura baṛa prīta*  
*pūrve jena śrī-kṛṣṇa-arjuna dui mita*  
*kṛṣṇa-kathā paraspara rahasya-prasaṅge*  
*niravadhi purī-saṅge thāke prabhu raṅge*

**One day, Mahaprabhu went to Puri Goswami’s math and sat down close to Paramananda Puri. The Lord loved Paramananda in the same way that Krishna previously loved His friend Arjuna. Mahaprabhu spent a lot of time with Paramananda, discussing esoteric matters related to Krishna. (Cbh** [**3.3.232-234**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/3.232)**)**

Paramananda Puri, popularly known as Puri Goswami or Puri Gosai, was a disciple of Madhavendra Puri and godbrother of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s spiritual master, Ishwara Puri. Amongst all of Mahaprabhu’s sannyasi associates, none were dearer to Him than Paramananda Puri and Svarupa Damodar.

Next to Paramananda’s math was a well, but the water had become muddy and was unusable. Being omniscient, Mahaprabhu knew that this water was not potable, but he asked Paramananda about it anyway, having the intention of glorifying its sanctity. Paramananda said, “What can be said of this miserable well? Its water is too muddy to use.”

Mahaprabhu answered, “It seems that Jagannath must have become miserly about giving liberation. He knows very well that any living being who touches or drinks the water from Paramananda’s well will be freed from all his sins and thus liberated. He must have made the water of this well undrinkable in order to discourage anyone from taking it. That way, no one gets liberation.”

Mahaprabhu then stood up and prayed with His arms upraised, asking Lord Jagannath to be merciful to the jivas:

*jagannātha mahāprabhu more ei vara*  
*gaṅgā praveśuk ei kūpera bhitara*  
*bhogavatī gaṅgā je āchena pātālete*  
*tāṅre ājñā kara ei kūpe praveśite*

**Lord Jagannath, grant me this boon: Let the Ganges enter into this well. Please order the Bhogavati Ganga, which travels through the underworld, to flow into this well. (Chaitanya Bhagavata** [**3.3.235-6**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/3.235)**)**

A little later, Mahaprabhu and all the devotees returned to their homes. The next morning, when some of them came to Puri Gosai’s math, they saw to their amazement that the well’s water had become pure and clear. They joyfully shouted the names of the Lord so loudly that the heavens began to reverberate with the sound. Paramananda Puri himself became completely absorbed in divine consciousness and fell to the ground, as though unconscious. Everyone could understand that the Lord had blessed the well and that the Ganges had entered into it at His request. The devotees circumambulated the well, singing the Lord’s holy names.

Word quickly reached Mahaprabhu, who upon hearing what had happened, immediately came there. When He came and saw the purified water, the Lord said,

*e kūpera jale je karibe snāna pāna*  
*satya satya haiba tāra gaṅgā-snāna phala*  
*kṛṣṇa-bhakti haibo tāra parama nirmala*

**“Listen, everyone. Anyone who drinks the water of this well, or bathes in it, will most certainly get the benefits that come of bathing in the Ganges itself. Not only that, but he will get pure devotion to Krishna.” (Cbh** [**3.3.251-252**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cb-antya/3.251)**)**

The devotees joyfully began to sing the Holy Names in kirtan when they heard the Lord make this pronouncement. The Lord then did exactly as He had advised them and drank water from the well and then doused Himself in it.

Ever since this pastime, Paramananda’s well was famous in Jagannath Puri. Even so, in time it once again became in need of repairs and cleaning. This important service was done by Bhaktivinoda Thakur in 1904, with financial assistance from one of his devotees, a lady named Mrinalini Das. The well was not only cleaned, but a concrete platform was built around it. After this repair work was done, a stone plaque was placed inside the well rim with an inscription giving the year and the name of the donor.

The water from this well still has a good reputation throughout the town. Gaudiya Vaishnavas sprinkle it on their heads and drink it in the hope of attaining Krishna bhakti. Many maths use it on special occasions for ritual bathing of their deities (abhishek). Thus one often sees processions of devotees chanting the Holy Names coming to this well with containers made of silver or gold to ceremoniously collect water for this purpose.

Though the place where Paramananda lived is indicated by the well, there is nothing else there to remind us of this associate of the Lord or the daily visits the Lord made there. Devotees are advised to simply take water from the well and pay their prostrated obeisances in the dust of this place in memory of him.

## Jhanj Pita Math

This math is situated in the Kundhei Bent Sahi, or Suar Para. According to tradition, it has a connection to the great 16th-century Vaishnava Narottam Das Thakur. Sundarananda’s report is based on information received from the Cuttack sollicitor, Sharat Chandra Ghosh. He gave the following account according to some ancient papers pertaining to the Math’s history that he found: It is said that when Nityananda Prabhu came to Puri, this part of the town was not yet built up. Nityananda came here with some of the town’s children and sang and danced with them to the sound of the Holy Names. Then when Narottam Das travelled through east India to visit all the sites of Mahaprabhu’s pastimes and came to Jagannath Puri, he came to this place and immediately felt ecstatic love for Mahaprabhu. Narottam was accompanied by a disciple named Seva Das,\[cxxxix\] who cared for Narottam Das, bringing him back to external consciousness. Narottam then told him of the glories of that particular spot and told Seva Das to remain and do his bhajan there.

Seva Das was particularly attached to chanting the Holy Names aloud with large cymbals or whompers, known as *jhāñja*. The word *piṭā* means “clanging,” so the name Jhanj Pitha was given to the math established by Seva Das as a result of his way of worshiping the Lord.

One year, another of Narottam Das’ disciples came to Jagannath Puri with three Shalagram Shilas and the Radha Kanta deity installed by Narottam himself in Kheturi. The Gajapati king gave land around the Math to provide an income for the Radha Kanta’s service. He also arranged for one pot of Jagannath prasad to be sent to the Math every day for the devotees living there. When the British took over the government of Orissa in 1804, then they established an annual stipend of Rs. 550 for the running of the math.

Seva Das was succeeded (after several generations) by Jagannath Das, who served the deities nicely. His disciple Bhagavan Das who followed him, however, was careless in his management of the temple and under him the annual stipend was stopped. In his will, Bhagavan Das named his disciple Krishna Das to succeed him, but Krishna Das tried to establish his authority while Bhagavan Das was still alive. As a result, the two ended up in court and ended up wasting all the temple’s possessions in the process. They sold off the deities’ jewelry and clothing, the pots and pans from the kitchen, and eventually even broke down the math’s buildings in order to sell off the bricks in order to maintain themselves and to finance their court battle. Krishna Das mortgaged the Math’s land holdings to a Brahmin money-lender from Mahapur in Puri district named Vrindavan Mishra. He received Rs. 500, but with a usurious rate of interest that spiralled out of reach in no time at all. Vrindavan Das also financed the court case in the hopes of getting a return on his investment.

Bhagavan Das died before the court case was resolved. In the meantime, Krishna Das transferred ownership of the deities and properties to a certain Fakir Satpati. As a part of the deal, Fakir Satpati made a verbal agreement to pay off the debt and also to finance the deity service and maintain Krishna Das for as long as he lived. Vrindavan Mishra considered this an attempt by Krishna Das to evade his liabilities, and took both him and Fakir Satpati to court, demanding the sum of Rs. 3500. The court decided in favor of Vrindavan Mishra and ordered Krishna Das to pay the sum of Rs. 4000. At the time, the Math consisted of nothing more than four dilapidated buildings, one for the deities, another for the cooking and the other two for the Math’s two residents. Krishna Das then died, leaving the Math in this condition.

Vrindavan Mishra was left looking for someone from whom he could collect the Rs. 4000 the court had awarded him. He made friends with the surveyor of the area where the Math’s lands were and decided to claim them, arguing that Krishna Das had died without a successor. The police investigated and found that Krishna Das’ only movable possessions had been the Radha Kanta deities and a few wooden shutters. These were confiscated and a date for the auction was set.

At this point, however, Radha Raman Charan Das Babaji got involved. Through his disciples, he intervened with the local magistrate and managed to reinstall the deities back in their own temple where they could be properly worshiped while awaiting the auction. On the day of the auction, Charan Das’ disciple Advaita Das presented himself as a claimant to Krishna Das’ possessions and was accepted as such by the court. He was given the deities, but did not remain there long, turning over the Math to another godbrother, Nityananda Das.

When Charan Das Babaji left his body in 1905, the entire Math was placed under the administration of the Jagannath temple. At this point, Ram Das Babaji made a concerted effort to regain possession of the temple. The Jagannath Estate asked for Rs. 1000, but finally accepted Rs. 600 for the property. Nityananda Das then turned the Math over to Ram Das Babaji Mahashay in due form.

Under Ram Das’ direction, deities of Nitai Gaura and Radha Krishna were placed on the altar, a new temple and natya mandir were built, and the devotees’ quarters repaired.

Every year at Rathayatra time, the disciples and grand-disciples of Ram Das Babaji come to the Jhanj Pita Math and participate in the festival in a unique way by reenacting the lilas of Mahaprabhu through the text of the Chaitanya Charitamrita. On the day before Gadadhar Pandit’s disappearance day, the devotees of this sampradaya are greeted by the devotees of the Radha Kanta Math in order to reenact the meeting of Mahaprabhu’s Bengali and Orissan devotees as described in the Chaitanya Charitamrita. They are led to the Gambhira where the devotees sing chapter 10 of the Antya lila, describing the gifts the Bengali devotees would bring for Mahaprabhu. Some representatives of the families of Mahaprabhu’s associates are usually present in order to bring the very things that their ancestors brought for Mahaprabhu.

The next day, these devotees go to Tota Gopinath where they sing the visit of Nityananda to Gadadhar, bringing a gift of fine rice from Bengal. This kirtan is based on Chaitanya Bhagavata, Antya 8. They then follow Lord Chaitanya’s Rathayatra pastimes as described by Krishna Das Kaviraj.

Devotees from the Jhanj Pita Math also participate in the Jagannath Deva’s puja by singing at mangal arati and in the evening at Boro Sringar.

Charan Das Babaji lived from 1853-1905. His great talent was for kirtan, and for making up songs that reflected his mood. He especially shone in Puri, where his kirtans were like a window into Mahaprabhu’s lila.

## Narayan Chata Math

About 200 meters along the Grand Road from the Singha Dwar stands the Narayan Chata Math. This is a very old temple and has a long-standing connection to the Jagannath temple. The deities are named Subha Lakshmi and Narayan Deva. According to the descriptions of the *Siddhārtha-saṁhitā*, the four-armed form in this temple is Madhava because of the way the four symbols are held in His hands. Lakshmi Devi resides on his chest and another figure of Garuda stands below the Lord’s lotus pedestal. Tradition holds that King Ananga Bhima Deva founded this temple in order to ward off any inauspiciousness that could affect reconstruction work on the Jagannath temple.

The service of these deities has changed hands several times. During the time of King Prataparudra, it was given to Gaudiya Vaishnavas, but was turned over to the Ramanuja Sampradaya for some time before returning to Gaudiyas. At one time, the math had a great deal of land given by the royal family, but careless management resulted in the gradual dwindling of these resources. In later times the Jagannath Deva Estate took over the management of the temple, but provided only a pittance for its maintenance. The deities were worshiped with water and tulasi on a broken down altar underneath a banyan tree on the property.

About 120 years ago, Sarvabhauma Jagannath Das Babaji’s disciple Gopi Charan Das Babaji came to Puri and saw the desperate condition of the temple and became very distressed. He took over the service and maintained it by begging. Through him, Ramchandra Arhya, a wealthy former resident of Calcutta then living in Puri, constructed the temple that is seen there today.

Gopi Charan Dasji used to serve the deities with madhukari, begging for whatever rice was given him, whether sun-parched or parboiled. He would cook it himself, offer it to the deities and distribute it to whoever came, invited guests or beggars, and only take what was left for himself. One day, a certain Raghunath Das Babaji came and criticized him for offering parboiled rice to his deities, for scripture specifically says that such rice cannot be offered as bhoga. Gopi Charan Dasji answered, “I offer the deities whatever is given to me. I have no control over that.” Raghunath Dasji countered by saying, “If the Deity is in control, then He will most certainly arrange for sun-dried rice.” Thereafter all the temple’s donors stopped giving parboiled rice. Raghunath Das was given the name Karta (“the boss”) Babaji. He disappeared at Har*i* Das Thakur’s samadhi temple.

Gopi Charan Dasji often distributed Jagannath’s pakhal (water rice) prasad to the poor. Once, he ran out of prasad, leaving some people hungry. One of these people became angry and threw an empty clay prasad container at the Babaji, cutting him. Despite being wounded in this way, Gopi Charan Dasji did not become in the least angry. A rich householder from Serpur in Mymensingh, Govinda Kumar Chaudhury, witnessed his tolerance and was so impressed that he arranged for three rupees to be given daily from his estate. After his death, this sum was reduced by his descendants, but was nevertheless maintained for many years. There is a stone inscription in the enclosure wall that says, “These deities are being maintained through the donations of the late Govinda Kumar Chaudhury.” Besides these gifts, the Narayan Chata Math also had some land holdings.

## Sri Kunja Math

This math is a few hundred metres southeast of the Siddha Bakul Math. It was founded in the first half of the 17th century by Rasikananda Prabhu, the famous disciple of Narottam Das Thakur’s associate, Shyamananda Prabhu. Rasikananda, or Rasika Murari, had a great influence on spreading the chanting of the Holy Names in northern Orissa, going from door to door, engaging people in Krishna’s service, inviting them to chant and holding kirtan festivals in their homes all over the land.

Once, Rasikananda decided to attend the Rathayatra and was making haste toward Puri with a group of companions and offerings for the Lord. He had left late, however, and did not make it to the holy city in time to see the beginning of the festival. In fact, by the time he had reached the outskirts of the town, Jagannath, Balaram and Subhadra had already made it as far as Balgandi, the halfway point between the Boro Deul and Gundicha. There, however, the chariots had become stuck and were resisting all efforts to move them.

Hundreds and thousands of pilgrims pulled on the carts’ ropes, but were unable to budge them even an inch. The king himself was present and he marshalled his horses and elephants in an attempt to dislodge Lord Jagannath’s chariot, but all his efforts had been stymied.

Lord Jagannath spoke to one of his servants, a Mudirath, saying that He would not move until Rasika Murari had touched His chariot. As soon as he heard this message, the king engaged a number of his men to look for Rasikananda in the crowd. He and many other devotees followed them, hoping to catch sight of the saint. They finally found him at Atharo Nala. The king paid his obeisances to Rasikananda and glorified him, informed him of the situation, and brought him back to Balgandi.

Rasikananda prostrated himself before the lotus-eyed Lord. He then gave the Lord the gifts he had brought – food, silk cloth and ornaments. As he looked at the Lord, tears poured from Rasikananda’s eyes. He began to dance and sing and his companions accompanied him in sankirtan.

The Pratiharis came to Rasika Murari and said, “We won’t be able to get the chariot to move unless you pull on the rope.” Rasika then went to the chariot and leaned his head against the wood. The moment his head touched it, the three raths began to advance. This time, they were pulled as far as Bali Nahar, where they stayed for nine days.

Rasikananda met with all the spiritual leaders of the town. The Vaishnava, Brahmins and sannyasis were all attracted to his charismatic spirituality, and everyone recognized him as a great soul. He visited all the holy places and sites of Mahaprabhu’s pastimes.

Lord Jagannath used to have a flower garden in the Bali Sahi district, one of the places that provided Lord Jagannath with fruits and flowers. Rasikananda asked for this place to be given him to establish a math. He also asked for the beautful deity Bata Krishna, which was kept in a shrine on the Kurma Berha wall, to be given him for worship in the new math. The king not only granted Rasikananda these two requests, but also provided a land endowment for the ongoing service of the deity.

Rasikananda Prabhu inaugurated the Math, installing deities of Radharani and Lalita in the temple on either side of Bata Krishna, whom he renamed Radha-Rasika Raya. Being established in a flower garden, the math was first known as Phul Tota Math. Exactly when the name was changed to Sri Kunja Math is not known, but the difference between a *kuñja*, or forest bower, and a *ṭoṭā*, or flower garden, is minimal, as both are places where Krishna enjoys pastimes with Radharani.

Rasikananda’s biography, *Rasika-maṅgala*, the following summary is given of these events in his life:

*rājā-sthāne bhūmi māgi’ dakṣiṇa pāraśe*  
*phula-ṭoṭā maṭha kaila manera hariṣe*  
*bāra hāta tina dhoṇḍā mālā haya niti*  
*niyojita kaila daśa pāṅca sevāita*  
*daśa-biśa ābaṛā kaila bhoga nirṇe*  
*grāma niyojita kari dila dvija-sthāne*  
*aneka dilena dravya sarva-dvija-gaṇe*  
*vastra-ābharaṇa dila kṣetra-vāsi-jane*  
*sabākāre santuṣṭa karilā rasikendra*  
*bidāya karila prabhu manera ānande*

**\[Rasikananda\] asked the king to give him land to the south of the temple and joyfully established a math in the Phul Tota. \[In the festival that marked the math’s opening, Rasikananda\] engaged between five and ten servants to make fifteen feet of flower garlands for the guests. Between ten and twenty mounds of rice were cooked to offer in bhoga, . He gave numerous gifts of clothes and jewelry to the Brahmins and residents of Sri Kshetra. In this way Rasikananda made everyone happy, politely bidding them all good day personally. (*****Uttara-vibhāga*****, 10.59-63)**

The disappearance days of both Shyamananda Prabhu and Rasikananda Prabhu are celebrated at this Math, which is managed by Rasikananda’s descendants who live at Gopiballabhapur in Midnapore district (West Bengal). The math mahant is thus the present-day Mahant of Gopiballabhpur, Krishna Kesavananda Deva Goswami. The math had extensive land possessions in Midnapore, Balesore and Puri districts. The local math manager is called an adhikari. Since the mahant could not be present everywhere, the adhikari has the right to make disciples. During Sundarananda’s time, the adhikari was named Tulasi Charan Das.

There is a shrine with a murti of Rasikananda, but the temple has no deities of Mahaprabhu. The temple room itself dates from Rasikananda’s time, but the other buildings, including the Jagamohan, are more recent. There is a stone plaque commemorating the rich donor who built it, a landowner from Palasi village in Midnapore, but repeated coats of whitewash have obscured his name.

Here too, the residents tell the sad story of a manuscript library that was lost to the negligence of unqualified caretakers. Formerly, this math provided profuse amounts of fruits and flowers for Jagannath’s service; despite the reduced size of the gardens and neglect, it is still able to send garlands on a daily basis, and on special occasions also. The Singhari Pandas used to receive an annual stipend from this math. There is a small samadhi shrine on the math grounds, dedicated to the memory of a Goswamini from Gopiballabhpur who died while on pilgrimage in Sri Kshetra.

The temple is clean, but suffers from a lack of resources. Much of the math property has been lost as a result of encroaching neighbors. The current adhikari would like to build up a nice garden again so that the math may live up to its name.

## Sri Nandini Math

In the territory of Gauda, at a place called Jangali Tola, is the chief seat of the Sakhibhava Vaishnavas, who dress like girls and act as religious guides for some of the impure tribes. The order is said to have been established by Sita Thakurani, wife of Advaita, but so far as I can learn, has not spread to any distance, not to any considerable number of people. The two first persons who assumed the order of Sakhibhava were Jangali, a Brahmin, and Nandini, a Kayastha. Jangali was never married and it is only his pupils that remain in this district, and these are all Vaishnavas who reject marriage.”\[cxl\]

## Kotha Bhoga Math

This math is situated in the Dol Mandap Sahi, directly to the east of the temple. Tradition has it that Advaita Acharya established this math. The temple houses the following deities: a six-armed form of Lord Chaitanya, Radha-Krishna deities known as Radha-Vrindavan Chandra, and Lord Jagannath.

The name of this math comes from one of the types of food offering made to Lord Jagannath in the main temple, Kotha Bhoga and Chatra Bhoga. Kotha Bhoga refers to those offerings that are financed by Lord Jagannath’s own land holdings and the state treasury. At one time, devotees of this math administered these offerings, and this is how it got its name. These days, however, not many people are willing to call this a math, as there are no longer any renounced devotees living there.

The owners of this math are descendants of Advaita Acharya with connections to Shantipur, but they make their headquarters here. The mahant in 1945 was Ras Bihari Goswami. Like many other caste Goswamis, he spent a great deal of time travelling from one disciple’s home to another.

This math has a long-standing relation with the above-mentioned Nandini Math. Traditionally, its mahant decorates the new mahant of the Nandini math with golden bangles during his investiture ceremony.

The deities’ temple is a small and unimposing structure, though the adjoining residential building is much larger. The householder mahants live in this building and rent out many rooms. Money for the temple comes from its land holdings, rent income and disciples’ donations.

## Suna Goswami Math

This math is in Bali Sahi. It supplies flower ornaments like alaka and chausara for Chandan Yatra, polish for the Ratnavedi at the time of banak lagi. It supplies adhivas jal from the well of Sitala for the Snana Purnima rituals, offers panti bhoga to Dola Govinda at the time of the Agni Utsava. The Mahant of this math is also the mahant of the Darpa Narayan Math.

## Sri Bali Math

This math is in Markandeshwar Sahi, next door to the Boro Oriya Math. The founder of this math was Abhiram Thakur, one of the twelve Gopals who were the intimate associates of Nityananda Prabhu. The deities served here are Radha-Krishna, Patita Pavan Sri Jagannath, Radha-Madan Mohan (the *vijaya-vigraha*, or travelling deities) and Shalagram Shila. The main deity is Abhiram Gopal. The deities were previously housed in a straw hut, but later a brick temple was built. The Math’s mahant told Sundarananda that other than the service to the deities, there was no other spiritual activity in the temple.

The parampara at the time Sundarananda visited (their dates are uncertain) –

Madhavananda Das, Sridhar Das, Raghunath Das, Abhiram Das. The Nat Mandir was built by Sridhar Das’ disciple, Hare Krishna Das.

## Some other Maths of the Gaudiya line

There are a number of other maths founded my Gaudiya Vaishnavas that have fallen into desuetude. Some of these are no longer existing in any form, others have lost any semblance of religious practice or orthodoxy. The Sri Lalita and Sri Vishakha Maths are situated next to each other not far from Markandeya Sarovar. Another math stands on the banks of the Markandeya Sarovar, the Haveli Math. There are deities of Radha Shyamasundar, Radha Rasika Raya and Gaura Nityananda. The math is a branch of the Ganga Mata Math and is run by an adhikari.

There is a Khajuria Math in Markandeya Sahi. It once had a nice garden attached to it. There are deities of Radha Shyamasundar, but none of Mahaprabhu. This math had a medium-sized land endowment. The Radha Damodar Math is found in the Harchandi Sahi, on the left side of the road on the way to Paramananda Puri’s well. Next to it is a small building called the Damodar Vallabha Math

## Chapter 31 - Gaudiya Maths in Jagannath Puri

As has already been pointed out, Sri Purushottam Dham has special significance for the followers of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Prabhupada Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur. Long ago, Srila Vyasa Deva predicted that this would be the center from which devotion to Krishna would spread out to the four corners of the world – *hy utkale puruṣottamāt*. For the disciples of the Gaudiya Math, this is true not only because Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu spent half His life here in divine ecstasy, relishing the Holy Name, but also because Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur, the founder of the Chaitanya Math and the worldwide Gaudiya Maths, took birth here.

All the unique features of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s pastimes were fully revealed in Puri Dham. This is why the incarnation of Gauranga’s mercy, Srila Prabhupada, decided to begin his worldly pastimes in that holy place. Puri remained very dear to Srila Prabhupada’s heart throughout his life. In 1933, he established the Purushottam Dham Parikrama. His last visit to Puri took place not long before his disappearance. In fact, he only left the Sri Purushottam Math on the ocean beach in Puri a few days before concluding his earthly pastimes.

In the years since his disappearance, many of his disciples and grand-disciples from all over the world have established maths and temples that beautify the town and increase its glories and the glories of the saints whose line they honor. In this chapter, we will try to describe a few of them..

## The birthplace of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur

To the south of the Narayan Chata Math is the Chaitanya Gaudiya Math, which marks the birthplace of Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati. Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and his family resided there from 1870-1874, while he was Deputy Collector and Magistrate of Puri. The house that was here belonged to the rich Calcutta businessman, Ramachandra Arhya, who built it on land leased from the Dakshin Parshwa Math.

This sojourn in Puri was a very significant period in Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s life. While staying here, he wrote *The Akhras in Puri* (1871) and *The Temple of Jagannath at Puri* (1871). These books were written in English, but have unfortunately become unavailable at the present time.

Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur appeared here at 3:30 on Friday, February 6, 1874, on the Krishna Panchami of Magh. The effulgent and beautiful child was born from the womb of Bhagavati Devi while Bhaktivinoda Thakur and the other members of the household loudly sang the names of the Lord. Everyone was amazed to see that the child’s umbilical cord was wrapped around his body like a sacred thread. His parents gave him the name Bimala Prasad in honor of Lord Jagannath’s divine energy, Bimala Devi.

Bimala Prasad was about six months old when the Rathayatra festival was held. That year, by Lord Jagannath’s desire, the cart stopped directly in front of Bhaktivinoda’s house and remained motionless there for three whole days. Under Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s direction, a kirtan festival was held in front of the Lord for this entire three-day period. During one of these days, Bhagavati Devi carried the six-month old baby before Jagannath. The child grabbed Jagannath’s feet and took the garland from around His neck. Bimala Prasad’s first solid food was Lord Jagannath’s prasad.

Saraswati Thakur only remained in Purushottam Kshetra for ten months, but returned many times in his devotional career, both to engage in bhajan as well as to establish the Sri Purushottam Math in 1922.

## Madhava Maharaj recuperates his guru’s birthplace

This house where Saraswati Thakur was born was reclaimed in 1974 after arduous efforts by one of Siddhanta Saraswati’s leading disciples, His Grace Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj (1904-1979). It now houses a Chaitanya Gaudiya Math with a beautiful temple building.

Though many obstacles had to be overcome in order to make this temple a possibility, Prabhupada’s dear disciple Srimad Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj, out of his compassion for the devotees, agreed to accept the service and undertook the effort to restore the holy site.

Madhava Maharaj often discussed recovering the site of his spiritual master’s holy appearance with his godbrothers, but most of them were unable to see how the dream could be realized, as there seemed to be insuperable difficulties to acquiring the property. Since Madhava Maharaj served in the Chaitanya Math until 1954, he at first tried to get Bhakti Vilasa Tirtha Maharaj to spearhead the attempt to recover the holy site. In 1965, they together wrote to the then Chief Minister of Orissa, Sadasiba Tripathi, and met with him and the Endowment Commissioner, Biren Mitra.

The Dakshin Parshwa Math was the owner of the land, but its mahant had leased it to the Arhya family for 99 years.This lease expired at around this time and the Dakshin Parshwa Math undertook legal proceedings to recover its rights over the property. The case went from the lower courts all the way up to the Supreme Court with the final judgment declared in the Math’s favor, confirming its ownership of the land and buildings. Unfortunately, however, the fourteen or fifteen tenants, who had been there for a longtime, resisted the sadhus of the Math when they tried to occupy the premises.

Eventually the mahant of the Dakshin Parshwa Math gave up any hope of evicting the tenants and so decided to cut his losses by selling the property with the tenants still in it. These complications discouraged most of the Gaudiya Math institutions from getting involved despite their evident interest. However, Madhava Maharaj was advised by his lawyer Ranganath Mishra to go ahead and buy the building, despite the problem presented by the recalcitrant tenants.

In Orissa, no property held in the name of a Deity (*devottara*) can change hands without the express permission of Orissa Hindu Religious Endowments Commission. With the cooperation of the Dakshin Parshwa Math, this permission was granted on June 28, 1973. Many people were involved in this process, including Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Maharaj, who made frequent visits to Endowments Commission, the Dakshin Parshwa Math and the lawyers’ chambers.

The process was not easy – before the Endowments Commission rendered its decision, another branch of the Gaudiya Math presented presented papers to the Dakshin Parshwa Math making a competing claim on the property. They enlisted the support of the Orissan Governor, B. D. Jatti, and many other prominent citizens. Madhava Maharaj was in Amritsar when he heard of the other claim and had to hurry back to Cuttack to deal with the challenge.

An appointment was arranged for Madhava Maharaj to meet Governor Jatti on Saturday, May 26, at 9:15 a.m. On reaching the Raj Bhavan, however, he and his disciples saw that the Governor was about to leave in the midst of elaborate official security arrangements. Undaunted, Madhava Maharaj immediately jumped out of his taxi, causing the Governor to stop his car and come out to pay his pranams to the great consternation of the security staff.

Governor Jatti learned of the appointment for the first time from Madhava Maharaj. Nevertheless, he put aside his other plans and discussed the matter with Maharaj. Impressed by his demeanor and divine personality, the Governor quickly came to realize that the opposing parties’ claims had to be false.

This was not the last hurdle that had to be overcome, however. The competing claimants attempted to stay the permission to transfer the property to the Chaitanya Gaudiya Math, and had to be defeated in court. After this was done, Madhava Maharaj finally gained the permanent lease to the property, but still had to face the problem of tenants who had no intention of moving. The members of the Chaitanya Gaudiya Math were obliged to camp in a room on the opposite side of the Grand Road while the tenants and the Math engaged in another court battle.

When one tenant finally vacated, the devotees were finally able to move into one room in the building. On December 15, 1974, Madhava Maharaj and a few bhaktas entered, carrying an oil painting of Srila Prabhupada and joyfully chanting the Holy Names in sankirtan.

The situation with the tenants did not improve immediately, even degenerating at one time to physically intimidation of the devotees. Nevertheless, construction work was started on a two-storey residence for the devotees of the Math. H. H. Bhakti Kumud Santa Maharaj of the Chaitanya Ashram in Gaurbat Sahi provided help and support to Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Maharaj, the secretary of the Chaitanya Gaudiya Math, who was charged with supervising the construction work.

The resistance of the tenants finally broke down and from the end of 1977 to the beginning of 1978, they vacated the premises one by one. Except for a single tenant in the northern corner, they all left the house. The holy site of the birthplace of Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Thakur was officially inaugurated in glory and splendor, with Bhakti Dayita Madhava Goswami Maharaj officiating, on Tuesday, February 28, 1978. His work completed, Madhava Maharaj was recalled to the Lord’s eternal pastimes not long afterward in the same year.

On March 24, 1980, the cornerstone for a new temple was laid at Srila Prabhupada’s birthplace. While the foundations were being dug, the devotees were were amazed to find that the holy earth possessed a fragrance of sandalwood incense. Srila Prabhupada’s birthplace has the same spiritual quality as he. The beautiful skyscraping temple, which houses Sriman Mahaprabhu and His alter ego, Jagannath Deva, was officially consecrated on February 5, 1982, on the holy advent anniversary of Srila Prabhupada.\[cxli\]

Of these successful efforts to reclaim the founder-acharya’s birthplace, H. H. Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Maharaj writes: “If one is sincere, then by the grace of Guru, the Vaishnavas and the Supreme Lord, one can acquire the right to perform any type of seva. Srila Vishwanath Chakravarti tells a parable to this effect in his commentary on the Gita: There once was a sparrow who lived by the seashore. On the beach, the tiny bird lay a clutch of eggs, so small that they were hardly perceptible to the eye. They meant everything to the sparrow and she would constantly fly around them.

“One day, while the sparrow was away seeking food, the swollen and foaming sea washed over the eggs and swept them away. When the tiny bird returned and discovered what had happened, she was overwhelmed with grief. She learned of the cruel role the sea had played in this tragedy from the other birds. The tiny bird repeatedly begged the sea to return her eggs, but the sea did not heed her cry.

“The sparrow then made a vow to dry up the entire ocean. She repeatedly dove into the sea and brought water back to the land in her beak. The birds and other animals tried to persuade the sparrow to desist, but she would listen to no one.

“Narada Muni, who knows all languages, came to know of the sparrow’s impossible ambition and he too tried to restrain her. She respectfully bowed to Narada, but wanted to know why the sea would not return her eggs, since she had done nothing wrong. If she got her eggs back, she would, of course, immediately stop taking the water away.

“Seeing the tiny bird’s determination, Narada was filled with compassion and, by the power of his will alone, reached Garuda, the carrier of Vishnu, in heaven. He purposefully provoked the divine bird, Garuda, ‘While you are cavorting here in heaven, I am hearing that on earth the birds have no brains. Why is that?’

“Garuda wanted to know what he would have to do to dispel this idea. Narada asked him to see to it that the distraught bird got its eggs back. Immediately, Garuda flew angrily down to Earth and began fanning the sea with his mighty wings. The fury of their tremendous impact made the sea very afraid. In fear, the ocean personified came and stood before Garuda with palms joined in entreaty. Garuda thundered that he would not tolerate any insult to the birds and that the eggs of the sparrow would have to be returned. The frightened sea searched around for the eggs and returned them to the sparrow.

“The tiny bird was not strong but its perseverance and determination won the compassion of Narada and the grace of Garuda. Thus, the impossible was made possible.”\[cxlii\]

The Chaitanya Gaudiya Math in Jagannath Puri particularly observes the Niyam Seva period, or month of Karttik. It also holds annual festivals at the time of Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati’s appearance day and during the Rathayatra.

## Bhakti Kuti (Iskcon)

Next to the Satasan Math near the Swarga Dwar is Bhakti Kuti, where Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur lived from 1900-1903, after retiring from government service. He was accompanied by his disciple Krishna Das Babaji, who acted as his assistant. Siddhanta Saraswati also often stayed with him during this time.

On the outside wall is a marble plaque with the following verse written by Bhaktivinoda Thakur himself:

*gaura-prabhoḥ prema-vilāsa-bhūmau*  
*niṣkiñcano bhakti-vinoda-nāmā*  
*ko’pi sthito bhakti-kuṭīra-koṣṭhe*  
*smṛtvāniśaṁ nāma-guṇaṁ murāreḥ*

**In order to remember the names and qualities of Krishna Murari, he who is known as Bhaktivinoda has given up everything to come here to the land of Lord Gauranga’s pastimes, taking shelter of a room in this cottage of devotion (*****bhakti-kuṭīra*****).**

While living at Bhakti Kuti, Bhaktivinoda Thakur wrote several books including *Bhāgavatārka-marīci-mālā, Harināma-cintāmaṇi* and *Bhajana-rahasya.*

Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati regularly read and give discourses on Chaitanya Charitamrita in the presence of the Thakur at Bhakti Kuti. The Raja of Cossimbazar, Manindra Chandra Nandi, lived in a tent on the seashore and took instruction in devotional service from the Thakur and Siddhanta Saraswati.

According to Krishna Das Baba’s *Bhaktivinoda-carita,* the famous Radha Raman Charan Das Babaji also came to visit Bhaktivinoda Thakur during this time. The two knew each other, as the Thakur’s siksha guru Jagannath Das Babaji was also the spiritual master of Charan Das’ guru. Bhaktivinoda had also put a great deal of effort into organizing Harinam sankirtan during the Calcutta plague in the early 1890’s, in which Charan Das played a big role. Nevertheless, the Thakur did not approve of the “Nitai Gaura Radhe Shyam” kirtan Charan Das was preaching and asked him to give it up.

Though Bhaktivinoda Thakur fully intended to live out his last days in Puri, engaging in bhajan, poor health required him to return to Calcutta in 1903.

Later, in 1922, Saraswati Thakur established the Purushottam Gaudiya Math at Bhakti Kuti in 1922 and devotees stayed here until the construction of the new temple in 1931.

Before Bhaktivinode left this world he wrote a will in which he left the Bhakti Kuti property in the name of the Bengali government. He stipulated that the property should be used for sadhus or sannyasis who wanted to make a math and engage in bhajan. Some years ago the Bengali government put the property up for auction. Many babajis and mahants participated in the auction, but Iskcon's Jayapataka Maharaj came out successful in winning the property.

As a result, Bhakti Kuti is now a branch math of the International Society for Krishna Consciousness. Unfortunately, the original building constructed by Bhaktivinoda Thakur in 1902 was in such bad shape that it had to be razed and a new building constructed in its place.

A beautiful temple and luxury guesthouse have been built on the property. The building is to have four stories when complete. At present it has about eight guestrooms. Small deities of Gaura Nitai and a life size deity of Bhaktivedanta Swami Maharaj are worshiped in the temple..

## Sri Purushottam Math

Saraswati Thakur first established the Sri Purushottam Math at Bhakti Kuti on June 9, 1922, installing a deity of Gauranga Mahaprabhu. He instituted an annual memorial festival at the Math in honor of Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur and Srila Gadadhar Pandit Goswami, whose residence at Tota Gopinath neighbors it. On July 17, 1931, he set the foundations for the new temple for the Purushottam Math on land that had been donated by the Maharaj of Mayurbhanj.

The Sri Purushottam Math is currently a branch of the Gaudiya Mission, whose headquarters are at the Bagh Bazaar Gaudiya Math in Calcutta.

At present there are nine buildings, which include the temple proper; the kirtan mandap; two guest houses, a long building that includes an office and the bhajan kutirs of Sripad Audulomi Maharaj, and Sripad Bhakti Prasad Puri Maharaj (Ananta Vasudeva Prabhu). There are also a kitchen, a small goshala, a building where most of the Math residents stay and, on top of a hill, the somewhat dilapidated bhajan kutir of Srila Saraswati Thakur.

The devotees here sing many nice bhajans for several hours each morning. As part of their morning sadhana they daily circumambulate Srila Saraswati Thakur's bhajan kutir and sing the song, "Jaya Radha Jaya Krishna Jaya Vrindavan..."

Things have recently been picking up for this important temple. Service to the deities is being carried out in an effulgent manner. More funds have come from donors and they have rebuilt and expanded the guesthouse facility. They also plan on remodeling the bhajan kutir of Srila Bhakti Prasad Puri Maharaj and making it very nice

The Math owned a great deal of property but the government took over some of it in order to build the large water tower that presently stands due south of the Math.

## Srila Prabhupada in Purushottam Dham in 1936

(from *Gaudiya* magazine, 14.35, 541-545)

At 2 o’clock in the afternoon of Sunday, March 29, 1936, Srila Prabhupada left Cuttack for Puri. He was accompanied by Ananta Vasudeva Prabhu, Krishna Kanti Bhakti Kusum, Paramananda Vidyaratna, Sajjanananda Brahmachari, Sundarananda Vidyavinoda and others.

At about 5.30 in the afternoon, Srila Prabhupada arrived at the Puri station where the aged Radha Govinda Das Babaji Maharaj, Tridandi Swami Bhakti Prasun Bodhayan Maharaj, Gadadhar Das Adhikari Bhakti Suhrit, Udaya Babu and many other devotees from the Puri area greeted and garlanded him. The abbot of Puri’s Uttara Parshwa Math, the venerable Govinda Ramanuja Dasji, sent his new motor car to the station, decorated with flower garlands, as a way of honoring the glorious sun of the Gaudiya Vaishnava world. We have witnessed many other such instances of the abbot’s respect for Srila Prabhupada in the past.

Hanuman Khuntia, a worthy descendant of Mahaprabhu’s associate Kanai Khuntia, was among the first to greet Srila Prabhupada once he had arrived at the Purushottam Gaudiya Math on the seashore. Srila Prabhupada was pleased with Sri Khuntia for his deep faith, the great friendship he has shown the residents of the Math, and for the help he has given to further the preaching of Bhaktivinoda Thakur’s gospel.

Srila Prabhupada talked with Khuntia Mahashay for some time, telling him about his various preaching activities and particularly about the meeting he had had in Cuttack with the Diwan (chief minister) of the Cuttack princely state. The Diwan had been impressed by the transcendental diorama exhibition held in Calcutta, and asked that Srila Prabhupada organize one of the sort for the spiritual education of the people of Cuttack, for such things had never been seen there before. Hanuman Khuntia was excited by the idea of holding such an exhibit in Puri as well.

The purpose of Srila Prabhupada’s arrival at the Purushottam Math was to initiate construction of a temple for Srimati Radharani on the Chatak Parvat. At present, three buildings adorn the Math grounds to make a beautiful sight on the beach: Chatak Kutir, Bodhayan Kutir, and the temple dedicated to the spiritual masters in the disciplic succession, Gaura-Gadadhara, and Vinoda Madhava. One can get a good view of the ocean from everywhere in Purushottam Gaudiya Math because of its high placement on the dunes.

Of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas’ three beloved deities, Madan Mohan, who presides over *sambandha-jñāna*, is already present in Puri as Jagannath Deva. Similarly, Gopinath, who presides over the *prayojana-tattva*, is present at Tota Gopinath, Gadadhar Pandit’s place of residence just nearby. Now our worshipable Srila Prabhupada has been encouraging his disciples to establish a temple to Radha Govinda, the presiding deities of the *abhidheya-tattva*. This is especially important to Srila Prabhupada, the stalwart representative of Rupa Goswami in our time, because Govinda was Sri Rupa’s own personal chosen deity. In order to insure that the work starts very soon, Prabhupada came accompanied by his disciples Amritananda Sevavilasa, Paramananda Vidyaratna, and other disciples experienced in construction.

At present, there is one other construction project already going on at the Math, a residence called Sadhu Nivasa, facing the Bodhayan Kutir. Srila Prabhupada has created several groups of devotees to preach the message of Bhaktivinoda Thakur by singing his songs in the villages of Orissa. As a result, whenever news of Srila Prabhupada’s arrival spread through these villages, many devotees, respectable citizens and important people come to Cuttack and then Puri for his darshan. Srila Prabhupada has therefore ordered that a guest house and kirtan hall be constructed in both places.

The devotees have made a garden in front of the Math where various fruits and vegetables, as well as Tulasi Devi, are grown for the service of the deities and the devotees. Yadu Gopal Adhikari (Yadumani Babu) works tirelessly in the garden to keep everything growing. Srila Prabhupada named the garden "Ananda Bag," because it gives all devotees pleasure), or "Yadumani Bag," because it brings pleasure to the Lord of the Yadu dynasty, Sri Krishna.

The elderly monk Sri Radha Govinda Das Babaji Maharaj has been preaching the Maha Mantra beloved of Gaura-Nitai and served constantly by Hari Das Thakur. Babaji Mahasaya is a senior Vaishnava and sincere servant of Srila Prabhupada. He is particularly well-versed in the Bhagavatam and Vaishnava philosophy. Babaji Maharaj distributes prasadi sweet rice in the residential neighborhoods of Puri and gets even the little boys and girls to sing the sixteen names and thirty-two syllables of the Maha Mantra. There is little doubt that everyone who hears the nectarean chanting from his lips will be purged of the poison of all the various recently-fabricated rhyming verses that are being sung throughout Orissa instead of the Maha Mantra.

Tridandi Swami Bhakti Prasun Bodhayan Maharaj, Sripada Gadadhar Das Adhikari, Phenapananda Brahmachari and other devotees have also taken Srila Prabhupada’s orders seriously and are attempting to preach Hari katha from door to door in Puri. On March 29th and 31st, Swamiji spoke on Krishna lila with a slide show in the houses of Ray Bahadur Girish Chandra Das in Chakra Tirtha. On April 1, he did the same in the house of Satya Das Goswami and on April 2, in the house of the zamindar Hemendra Nath Ray Chaudhuri.

In the evening, Srila Prabhupada listened to his disciples sing the songs of Narottam Das Thakur and Srila Bhaktivinoda Thakur in the Chatak Kutir. Srila Prabhupada created sankirtan associations as a preliminary step to preaching the philosophy of devotion through these songs. He himself especially relished hearing Ananta Vasudeva Brahmachari sing songs like *Amala harināma amiya vilāsā* from *Gitāvali* and

rādhā bhajane jadi mati nāhi bhelā  
kṛṣṇa-bhajana tava akāraṇa gelā

“If you have no appreciation for worshiping Radharani, then you have frittered away your chance to worship Krishna.” (*Gītāvalī, Rādhāṣṭaka,* 8)

On the morning of April 1, the topic of Raghunath Das Babaji of Hati Akhra,\[cxliii\] a renounced Vaishnava who lived at the time of Bhaktivinoda Thakur, came up. At the time that Bhaktivinoda Thakur started preaching in Puri, this Raghunath Das opposed his publicly giving discourse on the Bhagavatam since he had not been initiated. Raghunath Das was subsequently attacked by fever and the blessed by a dream in which Lord Jagannath appeared and told him that he would be cured by medicine given him by Bhaktivinoda Thakur.

Raghunath Das sent a message to the Thakur, who, in the true Vaishnava spirit, came humbly and respectfully to visit him. On his arrival, Raghunath Das said, “You have come. I know that most magistrates (*hākim*) would normally never come to see a person like me because they think, *hā kim*? (“Who on earth is he?”). In other words, “I am really something great and this other person is a nobody.”

Raghunath Das then spoke with Bhaktivinoda Thakur for some time and his previous opinion of him completely changed. Raghunath Das’ fever dissipated soon thereafter and from then on he held Bhaktivinoda Thakur in great esteem for the rest of his days. Of course, the sight of a great devotee can cure us of our material disease and give us pure love for Krishna, so this is only a small indication of Bhaktivinoda Thakur's glory.

It is said that this Raghunath Das was formerly a Naga sannyasi who later came into contact with Bhagavan Das Babaji of Kalna, by whose grace he was converted to Gaudiya Vaishnavism.

On April 2, Ray Bahadur Girish Chandra Das came to the Purushottam Math to see Srila Prabhupada. Srila Prabhupada told him about the five kinds of eternal relationship with the Supreme Lord Krishna. If we use Hari kirtan or transcendental sound in any way to promote our mundane relationships with other human beings or any kind of other material relationships, then inauspiciousness is the result.

In the course of his talk, Srila Prabhupada discussed the difference between the Chaitanya Bhagavata and the Chaitanya Charitamrita in their accounts of Mahaprabhu’s life. In the Chaitanya Mangala and Chaitanya Bhagavata, the emphasis is on Mahaprabhu’s supreme divinity and transcendence, while in the Chaitanya Charitamrita, Mahaprabhu’s true personality and His personal message for humanity are described in a most fascinating way. The limits of transcendence for those who are speculating on the basis of their mundane sense perception is the undifferentiated absolute. But in the divine transcendence there is a superhuman charm that leads the individual to eternally serve the supreme object of service.

Srila Prabhupada continued to discuss how the Supreme Person is complete (*pūrṇa*), more complete (*pūrṇatara*) and most complete (*pūrṇatama*). He is complete as Maha Vishnu or Narayan, in which form he displays 60 godly qualities. In the more complete form known as the *svayaṁ prakāśa*, he has 62 such qualities. The most complete form is called *svayaṁ rūpa*, and there he has 64 transcendental qualities. Srila Prabhupada used mathematics and astrological calculations to explain how the significance of the numbers 60 and 64 in relation to completeness.

About the darshan of Lord Jagannath, Srila Prabhupada said, “When we see Lord Jagannath with material eyes, He has no hands or feet. Unless you have spiritual vision, the Lord will hide Himself from you. Both the Holy Name and the Lord’s deity form possess transcendental senses. The atheist does not believe that the deity form can talk. They think that the story of Sakshi Gopal is all imagined. But though the Lord hides from the non-devotees, He cannot remain hidden to one whose eyes are smeared with the salve of love. The Upanishads have refuted the idea that the Lord has material hands or feet in the *apāṇi-pādo* verse (*Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad* 3.19); and with the words *javano grahītā*, they confirm the Lord’s transcendental senses. Ordinary living beings cannot perceive these transcendental senses of the Lord with their own limited sense organs. Just fourteen miles from Puri is the four-armed form of Alalanath. Mahaprabhu revealed a six-armed form there. Devotees should preach Lord Purushottam’s glories everywhere.”

After coming to Purushottam, Srila Prabhupada glorified Gadadhar Pandit Goswami for several days. This is appropriate, as he is non-different from Gadadhar. Srila Prabhupada said, “We are surrendered to Gadadhar Pandit. Srila Pandit Goswami used to speak on the Bhagavatam to Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and his associates on the banks of the Narendra Sarovar. Therefore, we should soon soon establish the Bhagavata Asan or Bhagavata Khanda on the part of the Purushottam Gaudiya Math property that borders the Tota Gopinath temple, where the discussion and culture of the Srimad Bhagavatam will go on constantly.

In the morning of April 3, Srila Prabhupada’s scholar disciple, Gaura Das Brahmachari, *kāvya-vyākaraṇa-sāṅkhya-tīrtha*, came from Kashi Dham, and Prof. Nishi Kanta Sanyal, M.A., came from Cuttack to visit their spiritual master. As soon as Srila Prabhupada saw them, he said, “Both of you are manifestations of Gadadhar Pandit, so you should always remain here in Puri and discuss the Bhagavatam.”

Srila Prabhupada said that since Mahaprabhu and His associates disappeared from this world, two greatly destructive ideas about the Lord have arisen in Orissa. One is that the preaching of devotion to Lord Vishnu resulted in the weakening of the Orissan empire. The second is the ignorant attempt of a certain scholar to minimize the supremacy of Srimati Radharani’s sweet loving service in favor of the majestic type of devotion. Prabhupada said that just as there is a stillness after a storm, so after this storm of false ideas, a peaceful time will again come when the concept of divine love taught by Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu will shine as brilliant as the sun.

The statement *utkale puruṣottamāt* means not only that Mahaprabhu’s message of divine love will spread well beyond Orissa’s borders, but that the whole world will take an interest in the doctrine of the Purushottam that is held in Orissa. It means that the teachings of Ramananda, in which the sweetness of Radharani’s service to the Lila Purushottam is recognized as supreme above all other spiritual achievements, will be preached throughout the world.

Just as devotees came to Nilachala from all over to take shelter of Mahaprabhu’s lotus feet and in order to preach his message, so too, with the coming of Mahaprabhu’s dear associate, Srila Prabhupada, devotees came from Bengal, Assam, Orissa, from the West and from the South just to hear Mahaprabhu’s message. Nishi Kanta Sanyal and Pandit Gauri Das Brahmachari were not the only ones to arrive on April 3. At midday, Tirupati’s Subregistrar Pantulugaru Y. Jagannathan, Bhakti Tilak, B.A., arrived at his acharya’s lotus feet. Bhakti Tilak Mahashaya is a highly educated Brahmin from Andhra. He has translated *Caitanya-śikṣāmṛta* into Telegu and all the songs of *Śaraṇāgati* into Telegu verse. He is a good speaker and writer in both English and Telegu.

Many other devotees came from Orissa, Bengal and western India in order to participate in the 100-day kirtan festival. We have heard that the two German devotees will also be coming from Mayapur.

## Siddhanta Saraswati spends some of his last days in Puri

About two months before entering his eternal abode, Srila Prabhupada went to Puri. He stayed there at his bhajan kutir near the beach. To all those who came to see him, he gave the warning: “Get busy and worship the Lord undeviatingly. Not much time is left.” His disciples heard him constantly repeat the verses of Rupa Goswami’s first *Govardhanāṣṭakam* and those of Raghunatha Das’s *Govardhana-vāsa-prārthanā-daśakam.*

Mahaprabhu Himself used to see Govardhan in the sand dunes by the ocean, and the Yamuna River in the blue waters of the ocean itself. For Him, the gardens in Puri were Vrindavan itself. Overwhelmed with the loving mood of Radha, Gaurasundara was day and night absorbed in the separation from Krishna, uttering the words:

*kāhāṅ mora prāṇa nātha muralī vadana*  
*kāhāṅ karoṅ kāhāṅ pāṅ vrajendra nandana*  
*kāhāre kahiba kebā jāne mora duḥkha*  
*vrajendra nandana binu phāṭe mora buka*

**“Where is the Lord of my life, Krishna, the flute player? What can I do to find him? Where is the son of Maharaj Nanda? To whom can I speak to of my distress? Who would understand me? Without the son of Nanda Maharaj, my heart splits in two” (CC** [**2.2.15-16**](https://vedarama.com/en/books/cc-madhya/2.15)**).**

With tears washing over his face, Srila Prabhupada would also recite these verses from the *Chaitanya Charitāmṛta* that revealed Mahaprabhu’s heartfelt emotions. In this way he would remain absorbed in Krishna consciousness. Srila Prabhupada remained in his cottage amongst the Puri sand dunes for the appearance day of Madhvacharya, Govardhan Puja, and the disappearance day of Srila Gaura Kishor Das Babaji. He announced that the refrains from the two *aṣṭakas* mentioned above were special mantras for worshiping Govardhan Hill:

*pratyāśāṁ me tvaṁ kuru govardhana pūrṇām*  
*“O Govardhana, fulfill every one of my wishes!”*  
*nija-nikaṭa-nivāsaṁ dehi govardhana tvam \|*

**“O Govardhana, please give me residence somewhere near to you!”**

Srila Prabhupada left Puri on December 7, 1936 and entered the nitya lila on January 1, 1937.

## Gopinath Gaudiya Math

The current acharya of the Gopinath Gaudiya Math, Bhakti Bibudh Bodhayan, recounts how the Gopinath Gaudiya Math came into existence:

“One day, I was cleaning Srila Guru Maharaj’s Bhajan Kutir in Mayapur when he suddenly expressed his desire to spend the rest of his life in Puri and to give up his body there. So in 1992, after searching for a long time all over the town, we purchased a small piece of land according to our means. But at that time, we were not able to arrange a proper place for him to stay on a permanent basis. So each year Srila Guru Maharaj would just come to attend the Rathayatra festival and spend a few days. Still we went on trying to arrange suitable accommodation for him.

In 1997, Srila Guru Maharaj went to Vrindavan and while there had a realization about Mahaprabhu’s instruction to Srila Jagadananda Pandit that *vṛndāvane jāiyo nā rahio cira kāla*, which means, “Go to Vrindavan, but don’t stay there for long.”

I was there at the time and Guru Maharaj told me that he did not want to disregard Mahaprabhu’s instruction, which he took as being meant for him. He repeated his order to me, “So arrange my place at Puri, I want to spend rest of my life time there under the guidance of Gadadhar Pandit’s kshetra sannyas.”

As a unworthy disciple, I arranged a room for him on the property in Chakra Tirtha and then accompanied him from Vrindavan to Puri on May 1, 1997. From 1997 until entering the nitya lila, Srila Puri Maharaj was constantly living the different pastimes of Sriman Mahaprabhu in the Gambhira. At night, I would see him talking with Lord Jagannath and Mahaprabhu. Sometimes I would interrupt him in the middle of one of these conversations with Lord Jagannath, but he would refuse to say to whom he was talking. But I understood clearly that he was speaking with Lord Jagannath.

Gradually, Guru Maharaj installed a deity under a shed with an asbestos roof. He felt unhappy because he was staying on the second floor of a nice building and lying down on a soft bed, while Lord Jagannath was living in austere quarters. He prayed to all of us that we prepare a nice temple for Lord Jagannath and Sri Radha Madana Mohan. Now my dearmost Godbrothers, Sripad Ram Das Prabhu, Sripad Govardhan Prabhu and Sudarshan Prabhus are going fulfill his desire, to make a nice temple on the beach. It is under construction now and hope that it will be open in time for his upcoming Vyasa Puja festival.

## Sri Chaitanya Ashram. Bhakti Kumud Santa

This temple located south of Purusottam Math and a little north of the Caitanya Saraswata Math on Gaurbat Sahi road.

## Sri Chaitanya Saraswata Math

Sri Chaitanya Saraswata Math is located near the beach a couple of kilometers west of Haridas Thakur's samadhi on Bidhava Ashram Road in Gaurbat Sahi. It has a nice three story guest house and a beautiful temple which is the home of Sri Sri Gaura Nitai. An unusual thing about the deities here is that Nitai is holding a danda. The deities and the temple were established by Bhakti Sundar Govinda Maharaj the disciple of Bhakti Rakshak Sridhar Maharaj on the day of Odhan Sasthi. They have a nice festival every year on this day and invite devotees from many different maths all over Puri.

## Chaitanya Chandra Gaudiya Math

This math, which stands next door to the Gundicha Temple, is one of the most significant Gaudiya Maths in Jagannath Puri. It is the headquarters of the Sri Krishna Chaitanya Mission founded by Srimad Bhakti Vaibhava Puri Maharaj.

The math is in the Ai Tota gardens, where Mahaprabhu Sri Chaitanya showed His mercy to King Prataparudra. During the Rathayatra, Sri Chaitanya came here reciting verses from the Bhagavatam that expressed Sri Radha's longing for Sri Krishna. In the ardor of His love, He almost fell down and the king came forth to hold Him up. Though the Lord was pleased with Prataparudra for his humble service to Lord Jagannath as a sweeper, He feigned anger to warn his followers against coming in close touch with wordly-minded people.

Again, with all humility, the king approached Mahaprabhu reciting the *Gopī-gīta* from Srimad Bhagavatam. This time he received the Lord's blessings through a warm embrace. The place where the Lord embraced Maharaj Prataparudra is where the Sri Chaitanya Chandra Ashram stands.

B. V. Puri Maharaj appeared 1913 in the village Fulta, five kilometers from Berhampur in Orissa’s Ganjam district He came from a family of Ramanuja Vaishnavas, but was initiated by Bhaktisiddhanta Saraswati Goswami in 1936 on Balaram’s appearance day. He took sannyas from H. H. Bhakti Sarvasva Giri Maharaj in 1966 and started the Sri Krishna Chaitanya Mission in Kakinada, A.P., in the same year.

The Chaitanya Chandra Gaudiya Math was opened in 1983. The international Krishna Chaitanya Mission has eighteen branch maths in Orissa, Andhra Pradesh and Europe.

This math has a nice temple with beautiful Radha Krishna deities and a large guest house. This temple is famous for giving prasadam to large numbers of visiting devotees, especially during the Rathayatra.

## Sri Nilachala Gaudiya Math

This math is on Gaurbat Sahi in Swarga Dwar, near Hari Das Thakur’s samadhi by the sea. It is part of the Gaudiya Vedanta Samiti. Bhaktivedanta Narayan Maharaj writes in his biography of Bhakti Prajnan Keshava Maharaj that Keshava Maharaj decided to establish a temple in Puri while visiting in 1948, but was not able to carry out the project at that time. His wishes were later carried out by his disciples, Tridandi Swamis Bhaktivedanta Vamana Goswami Maharaj and Bhaktivedanta Narayan Goswami Maharaj, who opened the math on Rasa Purnima at the end of Karttik in 1978.

Currently Srila Bhaktivedanta Acharya Maharaj is in charge of the Math, assisted by Sachidananda Brahmachari. The deities are Sri Gauranga Mahaprabhu and Sri Sri Radha Vinoda Bihariji. The temple welcomes devotees from all over the world, especially during Snana Purnima, Rathayatra and other festivals.

## Bhaktivedanta Ashram

Iskcon’s Gaura Govinda Maharaj helped to arrange for the purchase of this 40-acre property in Sipasirubuli, on the beach a few miles south of town. It was left vacant for a long time until a group of western devotees got the idea of creating a grihastha retirement community. They sold plots based on a time share scheme, but there were some unfortunate difficulties surrounding the development. Iskcon acharya Jayapataka Maharaj recently installed Gaura Nitai deities in a small temple and three or four brahmacaris now stay there to take care of things.

## Gaudiya Saraswata Ashram

This is the name of the amazing temple located north of Haridas Thakur's samadhi on Satasan Road. This temple founded by Srila Saraswati Thakur's disciple Srila Srirupa Siddhanti Maharaj is very popular. It has beautiful diaromas covering virtually every inch of the temple, grounds and inside of the boundary wall. The deity worship is very nice here. The temple has nice Radha Krishna deities, many Shalagram Shilas and a Shiva linga on an altar behind Radha Krishna. Siddhanti Maharaj was one of Siddhanta Saraswati’s most learned disciples, who wrote commentaries on the upanishads, Bhagavad Gita and the Vedanta. The temple has a strong tradition of giving nice discourses on the Bhagavatam that are well attended by many pilgrims.

## Purushottam Gaudiya Math

The Purushottam Gaudiya Math founded by Bhakti Vilasa Tirtha Maharaj is a branch of the Chaitanya Math. It stands in close proximity to Haridas Thakur's samadhi, to its north. This temple service is dedicated to Sri Sri Radha Vinode Bihari and a large guest house stands on the property.

## Chapter 32 - Maths of Orissan Vaishnava Sampradayas

## Boro Oriya Math

The Boro Oriya Math was established by Atibori Jagannath Das, who is known in Orissa as one of the Pancha Sakhas, or “five friends.”\[cxliv\] Jagannath Das was an associate of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu who translated the Bhagavatam into the Orissan language. He did immeasurable service to the spreading of Vaishnavism in Orissa, but because of certain deviations from the teachings of Mahaprabhu, his followers are considered by the Gaudiya Vaishnavas to be an apasampradaya, or heterodox sect.

From the accounts given by the residents of the Boro Oriya Math, its original buildings were formerly the palace of Maharaja Prataparudra’s chief queen, Gauri Devi, one of Jagannath Das’ disciples, who made him a present of it. This version has been confirmed in *Jagannātha-caritāmṛta*, Dibakar Das’ biography of Jagannath Das. Even now, when one enters the Math, it gives the impression of being an old palace or fort, with many walls to pass through before reaching the inner sanctum.

The Math’s deities are Radha and Krishna, Jagannath and Lakshmi Devi. Subhadra and Baladeva do not accompany Lord Jagannath. Deities of Shyama Raya, Gopinath and Lord Chaitanya in his six-armed form stand in the Jagamohan. There is a large courtyard containing Lord Krishna’s swing, or *jhulan*. During the Jhulan Yatra, Subhadra Devi comes from the main temple to visit the Boro Oriya Math. (photo opposite page 78 in Khuntia).

One thing that distinguishes the Boro Oriya Math from Gaudiya Vaishnava maths is the placing of the deity of Mahaprabhu, which is not kept on the altar in the deity house, but in the Jagamohan. In the Gaudiya Vaishnava maths of Puri, the murti of the spiritual master (such as Gopal Guru, Hari Das Thakur, or Mamu Thakur) is generally placed on a separate altar or shrine on the porch, while Mahaprabhu is placed on the main altar with other Vishnu tattva deities or on a separate altar equal to those of Radha Krishna and Lord Jagannath.

The Boro Oriya Math is still one of the wealthier traditional maths in Jagannath Puri. In 1950, it had an annual income of Rs. 50,000 from various rent-free land holdings. It is also one of the maths most involved in the Jagannath temple’s rituals; its duties are enshrined in the temple record, the *Mādalā-pañjī*. The Boro Oriya Math thus supplies the twenty liters of polanga oil needed every day for the temple lamps, at a cost of almost Rs 1,000. During the Anasar, the Math supplies a new applique canopy called Trimunda Chandua, and is also vested with the duty of cleaning the Ratnavedi before Rathayatra. Besides these services, it also supplied the pillows that were used in Pahandi, the black cloth to mother Bimala, and a special bhoga at the time of Rukmini’s marriage to Krishna. The mahant of the Boro Oriya Math dresses as a woman to clean the Gundicha temple, a tradition that, according to math authorities, was started by Jagannath Das himself.

## Jagannath Das’ life

Jagannath was born on the Radhashtami day in 1490\[cxlv\] in the village of Kapileshwarpur, about six miles west of Puri town. This village is one of the sixteen Shasans, that is, it is one of the Brahmin villages surrounding Puri founded by the Gajapati king Kapilendra Deva, whose leaders sit in the Mukti Mandap.

Jagannath Das was a Brahmin family of the Kaushika Gotra, which had the family title “Das.” Jagannath Das’ mother was named Padmavati. His father Bhagavan Das attained considerable renown as a speaker on the Bhagavatam in Orissan. King Purushottam Deva was particularly pleased with his delightful explanations of the Bhagavata philosophy and gave him the “Purana Panda” title. Bhagavan Das trained his son to follow in his footsteps as a Purana Panda. He started making arrangements for Jagannath Das’ marriage when he was twelve years old, but Jagannath asked to put off the wedding until after he had finished studying the scriptures. He never married.

Jagannath Das became an expert in his work as a speaker of the Bhagavatam. He went to the Sri Mandir and set up a place inside the Kurma Berha by the Bata Ganesh deity near the southern entrance where he could reach a large number of pilgrims visiting the temple. Because of his handsome appearance, sweet voice and wide learning, he was able to attract a substantial following.

Jagannath Das was still a young man at the time that Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu took sannyas and came to Sri Purushottam Kshetra with His associates in order to teach the world to seek out love for Lord Krishna. According to the *Jagannātha-caritāmṛta*, Jagannath Das’ first meeting with Mahaprabhu came when the Lord was visiting the temple. The Lord saw him lecturing on Lord Brahma’s prayers from the Tenth Canto. Jagannath Das got up from his seat and followed Lord Chaitanya as He and His other companions circumambulated the temple.

Not long thereafter, Jagannath Das went to Kashi Mishra’s house to ask Mahaprabhu to give him initiation. Since Mahaprabhu did not give initiation, He sent him to an Orissan devotee named Matta Balaram Das, another one of the Pancha Sakhas, who gave him diksha in Kashi Mishra’s house.

According to another account, Jagannath Das met Mahaprabhu in Jajpur while the Lord was on His way to Puri for the first time. Mahaprabhu took Jagannath Das with Him to Puri and after some time had Hari Das Thakur initiate him in the chanting of the Maha Mantra. After this, Jagannath Das returned to Jajpur where he started making disciples and translating the Bhagavatam into Orissan verse. While here, he began developing an independent vision of Vaishnava philosophy, in particular giving up following the example set by Hari Das Thakur, the acharya of the Holy Name. Gaudiya Vaishnavas cannot understand why Jagannath Das reversed the order of the Maha Mantra, chanting the names of Rama before those of Krishna, in contradiction to the teachings of the fathers of sankirtan, Gauranga and Nityananda Prabhus, and the acharya of the Holy Name, Hari Das Thakur.

## Jagannath Das’ Bhagavata

Jagannath Das’ Orissan Bhagavata is considered by many to be the jewel of early Orissan literature. It had a great influence in the standardizing of the Orissan language of Orissa, through its judicious combining of Sanskrit and local words. Its popularity in Orissa is comparable to that of Tulasi Das’ *Rāma-carita-mānasa* in North India and it is still worshiped in many Orissan homes. Every Orissan village used to have a small house or room known as *bhāgavata ṭuṅgī*, where villagers would gather to listen to recitations of Jagannath Das’ Bhagavata. Many of its verses have become proverbial and are cited frequently by people throughout Orissa.

The Boro Oriya Math continues to supply the Sri Mandir with copies of Jagannath Das’ Bhagavata and its members recite it to groups of pilgrims inside the temple every day. This Bhagavata has also been published in Bengali characters in the Midnapore district, which was politically a part of Orissa at many different times in history and where the culture and language are something of a hybrid of Bengali and Oriya.

Jagannath Das’ Bhagavata is not an exact translation. He added several and in many place contradicts the meaning of the original text, allowing elements of Mayavada to enter. In fact, the introduction of Mayavada into Jagannath Das’ writings can be explained by the general background of Orissan religious history. Buddhism had been very strong in Orissa for many centuries, and even after the turn to Vaishnavism with Ganga dynasty in the 12th century, elements of Vajrayana Buddhism persisted in the society, just as it did in other parts of Eastern India. The Orissan Buddhists considered Jagannath to be a manifestation of the Buddha. It seems that Maharaj Prataparudra even persecuted the vestiges of overt Buddhism in Orissa during the early part of his reign. Many of these Buddhists took shelter of Vaishnavism as a way of escaping persecution, but the Buddhist philosophy of *śūnya-vāda* found a home in the teachings of the Pancha Sakha, who combined Mahaprabhu’s path of bhakti with jnana and yoga.

Many elements of the Pancha Sakha doctrine have similarities to Baul and Sahajiya beliefs in Bengal. Like the Nath Yogis, they hold that the body is a microcosm of the universe in which the cosmic dance of the Supreme Lord plays itself out. They identify Radha and Krishna with the individual soul and the paramatma in the body. They conceive of the ultimate truth as Void, or *śūnya,* which becomes manifest in creation as Maha Vishnu. In his Bhagavata, Jagannath Das refers to Lord Jagannath as *śūnya-nirañjana, alekha-nirañjana, nirguṇa brahma* and *avatārī.*

Devotional practices like chanting the Holy Name are to be combined with the physical disciplines of Hatha Yoga and the cultivation of knowledge. In their writings, the Pancha Sakha identify Chaitanya Mahaprabhu with both the Buddha and Lord Jagannath. Jagannath Das does not overtly present all of the Pancha Sakha doctrines in his Bhagavata, though they are found in some of his other works.

Jagannath Das is said to have written a number of books besides his verse translation of the Bhagavata. These include *Ṣola-caupadī* (“Sixteen quatrains”)*, Śaivāgama-bhāgavata* (“The story of the Lord in the Shaiva Agama scriptures”), *Guṇḍicā-bije* (“The trip to Gundicha”), *Satsaṅga-varṇanā* (“A description of saintly companionship”), and *Goloka-sāroddhāra* (“Extracting the essence of Goloka”) and *Tulābhiṇa*. There are also a few titles of Sanskrit books that are claimed, to various degrees of credibility, to Jagannath Das.

## The title “Atibori”

Jagannath Das’s hagiographer, Dibakar Das tells how he was given the title “Atibori.” One day Chaitanya Deva asked Jagannath Das to tell him who he had been in his previous life. Jagannath Das answered, “You are the Supersoul, O Lord, and so you know everything already. Even so, I will tell you what I believe. Once I was meditating on Radha and Krishna and completely forgot my material body. I saw Radha and Krishna ecstatically gazing into each other’s eyes. They started to laugh and out of Krishna’s laughter I saw You appear. Then I was born out of Radharani’s laughter.”

*āpaṇa śrī-aṅga pāchoṛi kaśā basan aṅgu kāṛi*
